title: MHH Roundtable: Pre-Camp Thoughts
description: It’s a big week for the Colorado Avalanche with the start of training camp tomorrow and the first regular season game on the 2026-27 season just around the corner. Here are our thoughts heading into this busy time period. With Cale Makar’s contract extension now official, what expectations (if any) have changed for him and […]
fullText:
It's a big week for the Colorado Avalanche with the start of training camp tomorrow and the first regular season game on the 2026-27 season just around the corner. Here are our thoughts heading into this busy time period.

Adrian: I'm hoping the expectation shifts to a more reasonable long term outlook in terms of Cale's usage. That means not making Cale play 28-30 minutes often in the regular season. Breaking single-season wins records isn't as important as having your best players at their best during the playoffs. He's proven to be a game-breaker when he's fully healthy. Protect that.

Jess: A human being is not the same thing as a technology product at all, but I just got a new MacBook this summer after my old one just didn't cut it for school and work anymore, so, to use how I view investing in expensive technology pieces like that, you made the investment, so you better protect it. As Adrian said, that means accounting for the future, not just this year, and utilizing him accordingly, not having him play 28-30+ minutes every single night. Having a defenseman that can set and break records year after year is absolutely incredible to watch, but those records don't mean anything if he's not at 100%, or as close to 100% as he can be.

Jackie: Expectations have always been high for Makar and the new contract doesn't change that. He's half of the reason for Colorado to have any sort of chance in any given year and he has to perform regardless. Paying him 20% (for now) of the salary cap maximum doesn't really change things either, this roster has been made top-heavy and it still is right now heading into the final season of his contract paying $9 million this year. Makar signing his deal is more of a continuation of the current dynamic rather than anything that's changed.

Matthew: Any top-flight athlete will always have expectations set at the highest of highest bars. Even though Makar projected to be the NHL's highest-paid player a year from now, I don't expect the higher-dollar figure to move the needle in any way for his personal expectations. I also don't expect this to change for the team as a whole: he will continue to remain the team's undisputed number one defenseman in all situations through the years. If we're splitting hairs, the only blemish (and that's a term that's very loosely applied in this conversation), would be for Makar to re-establish some of his scoring touch on the power play . His goal-scoring output on special teams dropped from twelve goals in 2024-2025 to only four goals this past season. He's proven that he can put pucks in the net; doing so on the power play can only boost what's been a lackluster showing for the Avs these past couple years.

Jackie: I've always thought that the organization has a pretty good idea prior to training camp of what their opening night lineup looks like barring injuries, so I don't think going from six to four preseason games changes much. I'm more curious to see how the shortened camp impacts the group of older veterans. Is the rest beneficial or does the short time frame take away from a cohesion process?

Adrian: Yeah I'm with Jackie not much is earned or settleed as far as the lineup goes in a preseason action. It can help guys shift their position in line for a call up, but the opening-night lineup is more than likely locked down. I thnk the rest is beneficial for guys on the mend. Namely Cale Makar who seems to be taking rehab skates.

Jess: To echo both Jackie's and Adrian's sentiments, I don't think it'll have much of an effect on talking about the opening night lineup players. They all know how to take care of themselves leading up to the season, and while the preseason is nice to get ramped back up into game action, it's pretty much a glorified scrimmage for a lot of those players. For guys who are looking to maybe be in the conversation for a call-up this year, I'm much more interested in watching those guys.

Matthew: In prior seasons, I might have agreed that the Avs roster would largely have been a set and forget situation. However, the departures of Ross Colton, Jack Drury, Joel Kiviranta, and Valeri Nichuskin have created a unique opportunity for fresh new faces in the lineup, something that we haven't seen in an Avalanche opening night roster for some time. We got a taste of the Gavin Brindley experience last season; maybe he solidifies his roster spot this year. Perhaps Fedor Svechkov and Zachary L'Heureux, coming over from Nashville in the Drury trade, will be given an extended look with a solid showing on a shorter preseason schedule. I don't expect major shakeups coming out of preseason (barring injury), but a shorter preseason may be more of a motivator for players looking to be a long-term fixture coming into regular season play.

Adrian: Nope. Just waiting to drop the puck!

Jackie: Typically PTO candidates for the roster will skate with the team for a couple weeks before camp and since we haven't noticed any mystery guests one seems unlikely. I am curious, though, if they remain interested in Michael Bunting who is still unsigned as of this writing. But GM Joe Sakic isn't scared to add via the waiver wire or trade, which is probably where the Avs are monitoring for any new additions.

Jess: With the preseason this close to starting, I don't think so, but I don't think it's out of the question entirely, as Jackie said, Sakic isn't scared to add via waiver wire or trade, and the same likely goes for PTO signings as well.

Matthew: I think it's unlikely, but never say never. Sakic has always maintained that, if there's a way to improve, he will explore it. As Jackie said, Michael Bunting seems to be a possible avenue if the interest is there. It will be interesting to see if anything does materialize between now and the end of the preseason, and if it does, how that impacts other players that are vying for roster spots.

Adrian: I think the Avalanche's success will rely heavily on how they mitigate the loss of Valeri Nichushkin in their top six so my answer has to be Jaden Schwartz who was seemingly brought in with hopes of him being a second line player. I'm not convinced yet so I'll have my eyes on his role early!

Jackie: There might be several waves of experiments but for the first round of it I'm interested to see how the coaching staff views Zach L'Heureux and their approach to utilizing him. There's a wide range out outcomes and if he is an impact player could give the Avalanche lineup a different kind of energy they desperately need.

Jess: For guys who will be in the opening night lineup, I'm super interested to see how Jaden Schwartz fits into the lineup. I'm also really excited to see how Gavin Brindley looks, knowing what a year he had last year with the Avs and how great that fit was, and I'm excited to see how Zach L'Heureux fits in on this team as well.

Matthew: Having had my eye on Jaden Schwartz for a spell during his time in St. Louis, I'm intrigued to see if a more talented group around him reinvigorates him and, more importantly, whether he stays healthy. Schwartz has missed varying stretches of play—both in St. Louis and more recently in Seattle—with injury. Whether it's on Brock Nelson's line or a third-line option with Nazem Kadri, I will be interested in how the former CC Tiger adapts to his new environment.

title: Maurkice Pouncey, Emmitt Smith to be inducted into Florida-Georgia Hall of Fame
description: Florida football greats Emmitt Smith, Maurkice Pouncey among those to be honored at Florida-Georgia rivalry game.
fullText:
Maurkice Pouncey and Emmitt Smith will be inducted into the Florida-Georgia Hall of Fame on Friday, Oct. 30.

The Florida football greats will be inducted at 12 p.m. at the Chick-fil-A College Football Hall of Fame in Atlanta. Former Georgia standouts Brandon Boykin and Andre Hastings will also be inducted.

This year's rivalry game will not be played in Jacksonville for the first time since 1995 due to stadium renovations. This season, the game will be played in Atlanta, while the following year will be hosted in Tampa in 2027 before returning to Jacksonville in 2028.

Before Smith became the NFL's all-time leading rusher, he rewrote the history books at Florida. From 1987 to 1989, the running back finished his career as the school's all-time leading rusher with 3,928 yards and 36 rushing touchdowns.

Pouncey was a member of the Gators from 2007-09, including a three-season run in which UF posted a 36-5 record, two SEC titles, and the 2008 BCS national championship.

The consensus All-American and future 18th overall pick of the NFL Draft started in 39 games for the Gators. In the NFL, Pouncey earned 9 Pro Bowl selections over an 11-year career.

Reach Florida Gators writer Andrew Abadie at AAbadie@usatodayco.com or on X (formerly Twitter) at @AndrewAbadie. You can also find him on Facebook at Andrew Abadie Sports Reporter or on Instagram @andrewabadie_sports.

title: Shut up! Former champ sick of your ‘annoying’ criticism about UFC 332 fight card
description: UFC 332 was recently made official for Sat., Oct. 3, 2026 at Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. The promotion struggled to find marquee talent for the five-round main event and had to settle for the vacant flyweight title fight pitting Natalia Silva against Wang Cong. If there’s one thing fans (and fighters) hate […]
fullText:
UFC 332 was recently made official for Sat., Oct. 3, 2026 at Delta Center in Salt Lake City, Utah. The promotion struggled to find marquee talent for the five-round main event and had to settle for the vacant flyweight title fight pitting Natalia Silva against Wang Cong.

If there's one thing fans (and fighters) hate more than flyweights, it's women's MMA.

"About the criticism, it's a little annoying," former flyweight champion, Deiveson Figueiredo, told MMA Fighting. "But I'm sure that all the fighters the UFC put on the card are ready to have a great fight, you know? And what looks weak can become strong. I'm sure — especially me, man, I'm ready to have a great fight. I admit that I didn't expect [to co-headline], but there were some complications on the card, and I moved up to do the co-main event. I'm happy, man. Once again I see the UFC valuing me, giving me great fights, great cards, always fighting on the main card — when it's not main event, it's the co-main event."

Figueiredo battles bantamweight wunderkind Payton Talbott.

"He has excellence in striking," Figueiredo said. "But I see myself as a guy with more excellence. If I fight at my level, aggressively, I'm sure I'm going to go right at him, and with great chances of knocking him out. But I can also do the grappling style. I'm a guy who trains all areas, so anything can happen in this fight. I'm prepared to have a great fight against him."

The 38-year-old Figueiredo (25-7-1) needs a win in the worst way possible, having dropped four of his last five while getting stopped in two of those losses. To be fair, all four defeats have come against the best of the best, but "Daico" is facing a red-hot Talbott (11-1) coming off back-to-back wins over Felipe Lima and Henry Cejudo.

title: 49ers in review: We’re buying stock in the secondary
description: Plus, Nick Bosa, the running backs, and more
fullText:
As we get ready to turn the page to the Miami Dolphins, let's take one last look at the San Francisco 49ers' Week 1 undressing of the Los Angeles Rams.

What are some things that happened in Australia that could be things to watch for as the 49ers return stateside? What players stood out? Which play was the most impressive?

Let's officially close the book on Week 1 with our first game in review of 2026:

The returns of Fred Warner and Nick Bosa were the two biggest headlines for the defense heading into Week 1. Warner lived up to his standard, exiting Week 1 as the most impressive 49er in Australia.

Bosa, however, left a bit to be desired. While the 49ers pass rush created 14 pressures on 28 Rams pass attempts, there was little impact felt from the front four. Bosa was no exception, collecting just one pressure and one quarterback hit on 20 pass-rush snaps.

But surprisingly, it wasn't Bosa's pass rush ability that was the story; it was his play against the run. While the 49ers defense as a whole struggled against the run, allowing 122 yards on 29 carries, Bosa's performance especially stood out. Bosa led the 49ers with four run stops on 16 run-play snaps, responsible for a third of the 49ers' run stops on his own.

Bosa's pass rush ability will come around at some point as he's returning from the season-ending injury suffered in 2025, but if Week 1 run-stopper Bosa can show up consistently, it would only add depth to the already uber-talented defensive end.

Maybe what happened on Thursday night was a blip and Kaelon Black will never out-carry Christian McCaffrey again. But the fact that it's something that happened in Week 1 makes it significant.

Here's a list of games where a 49ers running back not named Christian McCaffrey has 14 or more carries in a game where McCaffrey played:

Elijah Mitchell, 18 carries – Week 10 2022

Elijah Mitchell 17 carries – Week 17 2023

Kaelon Black 14 carries – Week 1 2026

And Black was deserving of those carries. The rookie gained 65 yards on his 14 attempts, looking explosive with the ball in his hands, with his longest run of the night a 14-yard carry on the 99-yard touchdown-scoring drive.

While Black impressed in his debut, McCaffrey showed why he's still the top back in the offense. On four fewer carries, McCaffrey gained more yards than Black, with a 10-carry, 68-yard performance in the season opener. McCaffrey also added five receptions for 20 yards while Black finished with one for five yards.

This is likely the most interesting thing to watch over the next few weeks. Was it a coincidence that Black out-carried McCaffrey, or was it intentional?

Several position groups could have earned this spot. We just discussed the running back room. The receiving corps was just as solid. And Fred Warner's performance alone could have given it to the linebackers.

But I am going to go with the cornerback group as the inaugural position group of the week.

Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are as fearsome of a duo the league has to offer, and the 49ers cornerbacks held them quiet. Deommodore Lenoir was targeted four times against Nacua, allowing 28 yards on three receptions, with the biggest blemish being a 23-yard reception allowed. Other than that, Lenoir was solid against the Rams' top receiver.

On the other side, Renardo Green handled his business. When in coverage against Adams or Nacua, Green was targeted three times, allowing two receptions to Adams for 23 yards. But the lone time Matthew Stafford targeted Nacua with Green in coverage, Green hauled in the first interception of his career.

Jack Jones and Upton Stout contributed as well, with the duo targeted seven times against Nacua and Adams, allowing just two receptions for eight yards, with Jones having two near-interceptions but settling with a pair of pass breakups.

Because of the corners, Stafford completed just 60 percent of his passes, which is a pretty significant percentage for the quarterback from 2025. In the four games Stafford completed 60 percent or less of his passes in 2025, the Rams went 1-3.

The 49ers' cornerback play against Stafford and his top-two targets was just as important as anything else that led to the 49ers' 20-point win.

There are three very good choices for this category, with Brock Purdy having a trio of highlight throws going for scores. The first a beautiful deep throw to Demarcus Robinson for a 39-yard touchdown followed by a connection with Mike Evans taking advantage of a one-on-one in a goal line situation.

But this week's touchdown of the week goes to Purdy's third and final touchdown pass:

Slimebo's back in business 😤

📺 Netflix pic.twitter.com/D8bs7y89AJ

For multiple reasons, it earns the nod, so let's start with Purdy. He starts with an excellent slide to the right outside of the pocket the second he feels pressure. But then there's the throw. As he's rolling to his right, he puts the ball perfectly over a pair of Rams defenders, perfectly leading Deebo Samuel into the open spot of the end zone for the score.

And that's the other reason this particular score earns touchdown of the week: it's not any Deebo Samuel, but it's No. 19, Deebo Samuel. Nostalgia is what the Robinson and Evans scores are lacking. It was the perfect exclamation point for Samuel's return to San Francisco, closing a six-catch, 48-yard day with his first touchdown as a 49er since December 30, 2024.

Oh, and it was also the dagger in a rout of the Rams.

title: Giants news: John Harbaugh makes tweak for MNF amid Rams' game travel
description: The Los Angeles Rams are in the middle of another unusual travel plan . However, this time it is the opposing team making the adjustment. After a Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys, the New York Giants are heading to Los Angeles early for their upcoming Monday Night Football game against the Rams at SoFi Stadium. Giants head coach John Harbaugh is […] The post Giants news: John Harbaugh makes tweak for MNF amid Rams' game travel appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Giants news: John Harbaugh makes tweak for MNF amid Rams' game travel appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Los Angeles Rams are in the middle of another unusual travel plan. However, this time it is the opposing team making the adjustment. After a Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys, the New York Giants are heading to Los Angeles early for their upcoming Monday Night Football game against the Rams at SoFi Stadium.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh is changing the team's usual road game routine. The Giants are set to leave for the West Coast on Saturday instead of Sunday, which is their typical schedule for a Monday night game.

Giants insider Jordan Raanan broke the news on X, formerly Twitter, on Thursday.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"The Giants are traveling to Los Angeles on Saturday this week ahead of their Monday night matchup with the Rams. A tweak from John Harbaugh," Raanan tweeted.

Harbaugh's travel plan is a clear contrast to the Rams' approach in Week 1. Sean McVay's team arrived in Melbourne less than 24 hours before facing the San Francisco 49ers after a 15-hour flight and a 17-hour time difference.

Los Angeles scored in the second quarter but was shut out for the rest of the game. The Rams also went 0-for-2 on fourth down and gave up 20 straight points in a 27-7 loss. Losing Myles Garrett to injured reserve has also left their defense without its top pass rusher.

The Giants are coming off a strong 28-20 win over Dallas. Jaxson Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns, while adding 54 rushing yards. Cam Skattebo ran for 81 yards and a touchdown as New York finished with 165 rushing yards. The Giants also converted 9 of 10 third downs and held the ball for 36:40.

title: Mack Hollins revised incentives in contract
description: New England Patriots WR Mack Hollins revised the terms in his deal before the season with more difficult incentives to reach.
fullText:
New England Patriots WR Mack Hollins agreed to a revised deal before the season, which made the incentives clauses more difficult to reach, according to Spotrac. In the original deal, he had $300,000 incentives for 30, 40 and 50 catches, which are now at 47, 50 and 55.

Why it Matters: Hollins had 46 catches last season and presumably agreed to more difficult incentives to avoid being cut. He had four catches for 51 yards in Week 1, and he'll see a larger role with A.J. Brown on IR with his ankle injury. Hollins becomes a weekly flex option.

title: Why Blue Jays will have 'money to spend' in 2027 MLB offseason
description: This is an important offseason for the Blue Jays.
fullText:
Why Blue Jays will have 'money to spend' in 2027 MLB offseason originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Toronto Blue Jays did an excellent job of balancing a strategic buy/sell approach at the trade deadline.

It's helped them stay competitive in the American League while retooling for future seasons. The Blue Jays could fall short of expectations in 2026.

Just one year after reaching Game 7 of the World Series, Toronto is eliminated from AL East contention and fighting for its postseason life.

As of Wednesday morning, the Blue Jays are two games behind the Cleveland Guardians for the third and final Wild Card spot.

This offseason, Toronto's front office will have an opportunity to add key pieces to the roster thanks to expiring contracts.

"The good news for the Blue Jays is that George Springer ($24.16 million) and Shane Bieber ($16 million) will be coming off the books," Bleacher Report's Tim Kelly wrote. "They also moved off Kevin Gausman ($23 million), Jeff Hoffman ($11 million) and Daulton Varsho ($10.75 million) at the deadline. So there will be money to spend in the offseason."

Impending free agents and midseason trades will allow the Blue Jays to spend more than usual this winter.

MORE: Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski makes all kinds of MLB history with 1,000 pitches of 100 mph

However, the club's core is still intact, even with a down year from first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr.

"With Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Dylan Cease, Trey Yesavage, Ernie Clement, José Soriano and Louis Varland, the Blue Jays still have a good base," Kelly added. "They need to retool the rest of their roster in the offseason."

This will be a significant offseason for the Blue Jays, and the decisions they make could make or break their future status as a contender.

title: Malagò chaos as FIGC risk of Special Commissioner over election paperwork
description: The FIGC could be placed under a special commissioner after the legal battle over Giovanni Malagò’s election took another twist. ‘It’s absurd,’ warned predecessor Gabriele Gravina.The situati...
fullText:
The FIGC could be placed under a special commissioner after the legal battle over Giovanni Malagò's election took another twist. 'It's absurd,' warned predecessor Gabriele Gravina.

The situation is spiralling out of control, three months after Malagò won a landslide election to become the new President of the Italian Football Federation on June 22.

CORTINA D'AMPEZZO, ITALY – MARCH 05: Giovanni Malago, President of the Organising Committee for the 2026 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, speaks during the Paralympic Games Opening Press Conference ahead of the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Paralympic Games at on March 05, 2026 in Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Ozbot/Getty Images)

It was pointed out that he was not registered as a member of the FIGC before his candidacy, because he had until then been with the CONI (Italian Olympic Committee, which oversees all Italian sport).

He therefore lacked the legal right to be put forward as a candidate for the FIGC, a scenario that has gone through several appeals already.

CORTINA D'AMPEZZO, ITALY – MARCH 5: Giovanni Malago, President of the Organising Committee for the 2026 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, speaks during the mural inauguration ahead of the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Paralympic Games at the Cortina Paralympic Village on March 05, 2026 in Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy. (Photo by Linnea Rheborg/Getty Images for IPC)

It took another twist because current CONI President Luciano Buonfiglio announced that they have no choice but to void the election.

"In light of what was acknowledged by Attorney General Ugo Taucer, it is indisputably established that Malagò was not registered at the time of his application.

"If the FIGC had intended to waive this requirement, it should have expressly provided for it. As valid membership must be one of the requirements for eligibility to federal bodies, whether elective or appointed, the FIGC appears to have violated these fundamental principles."

The Consiglio Nazionale body will now discuss the matter, and could well void the election, putting the Federation under a Special Commissioner.

FIGC President Giovanni Malago (left) with coach Roberto Mancini (right): @coppa_canottieri via Instagram.

It is unlikely to happen until after Italy's match against Turkiye on October 5, to avoid repercussions on Roberto Mancini's tenure as coach, seeing as he was appointed by Malagò.

It does further create chaos around a Federation that is trying to prepare for co-hosting duties of EURO 2032 and dealing with a crisis of results after failing to qualify for three World Cup tournaments in a row.

ZENICA, BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA – MARCH 31: (L-R) President of CONI Luciano Buonfiglio, President of FIGC Gabriele Gravina and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin look on prior the FIFA World Cup 2026 European Qualifiers KO play-offs match between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Italy at Stadion Bilino Polje on March 31, 2026 in Zenica, Bosnia and Herzegovina. (Photo by Getty Images/Getty Images)

"This is absurd," noted former FIGC President Gravina.

"The credibility of Italian football must be defended from repeated invasions from those outside, who seemingly on a cyclical basis try to undermine the autonomy of the Federation.

"It's absurd just to think that the FIGC could be put under a Special Commissioner purely for this reason. There needs to be more respect for the Federation, President Malagò and its components."

title: Chargers sign two-time Super Bowl champion WR to practice squad
description: Marquez Valdes-Scanting has signed with his ninth franchise.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Chargers are looking for some help at wide receiver after a disastrous season opener against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chargers are signing veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling to the practice squad according to ESPN.

In all, four Chargers wide receivers are currently dealing with injuries. Ladd McConkey suffered a rib injury in Week 1. Elijah Molden and Derius Davis are also day-to-day and KeAndre Lambert-Smith has been placed on IR. Justin Herbert completed 17-of-27 passes for 209 yards, one touchdown and one interception on Sunday.

Valez-Scantling spent training camp with the Dallas Cowboys, but was cut just before the season. Last season he signed with the Seattle Seahawks, but was cut before the season. He then spent some time with the San Francisco 49ers and Pittsburgh Steelers during the 2025 season. He appeared in five games for both teams.

In 2024 he split time between the Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints. He caught 17 passes, including four touchdowns for the Saints.

Before that he won back-to-back Super Bowls with the Kansas City Chiefs. MVS appeared in 33 regular season games for the Chiefs. He caught 63 passes for 1,002 yards and three touchdowns over those two seasons. In seven playoff games he scored three touchdowns for the Chiefs, including a third quarter touchdown against the 49ers in Super Bowl LVIII.

He keeps getting chances because he has NFL talent, but he's also been plagued throughout his career by drops. For every clutch catch to send a team to the Super Bowl, he's had multiple miscues. Problems with drops have resulted in him bouncing around the league, unable to find a home since he left Kansas City.

The Green Bay Packers selected Valdes-Scantling in the fifth round of the 2018 NFL draft. He played the first four seasons of his career there averaging about 31 catches, 500 yards and three touchdowns a season. The Chargers are his ninth franchise in nine seasons and if he gets activated they'll be the seventh team he has played for in his career.

title: Barcelona scout 22-year-old versatile Norwegian attacker with 23 G/A – report
description: According to Swedish publication Expressen, FC Barcelona sent representatives to scout Bo Hegland during Djurgardens IF’s Allsvenskan clash with GAIS on Monday.Djurgården have emerged as contenders...
fullText:
According to Swedish publication Expressen, FC Barcelona sent representatives to scout Bo Hegland during Djurgardens IF's Allsvenskan clash with GAIS on Monday.

Djurgården have emerged as contenders for the Swedish title this autumn and currently sit seven points behind leaders IK Sirius. And, Hegland has played a major role in their impressive run.

The Norwegian matched the Allsvenskan assist record against GAIS, setting up Kristian Lien for the opening goal. It was his 15th assist of the season, bringing him level with the competition's record.

Hegland then made an even bigger contribution after the break, scoring the second goal as Djurgarden secured a 2-0 victory, taking his tally for the season to eight goals in 21 matches.

Hegland attracted considerable attention during the summer. The 22-year-old versatile attacker, who can play anywhere in the final third, received interest from several clubs and had recently turned down an offer from Anderlecht.

He has also been linked with Newcastle United, with his performances in Sweden continuing to attract attention from abroad.

Now, Barcelona have also set their sights on Hegland and had scouts present to watch the 22-year-old ace in action this past Monday.

The Norwegian star joined Djurgarden in 2025 from Moss and has a contract with the club until 31 December, 2029.

The 22-year-old is a versatile player who can operate as a central attacking midfielder or a centre-forward, while he has also featured on the flanks on several occasions in his career.

Barcelona have previously monitored young talent in the Allsvenskan and have already looked to Djurgarden for emerging players.

As recently as 2023, Barcelona attempted to sign Lucas Bergvall from the Swedish outfit.

The Swedish midfielder ultimately chose a different route, joining Tottenham Hotspur in January 2024.

Barcelona's reported presence at Monday's match suggests that Hegland is now another Djurgarden player attracting attention from the La Liga champions.

However, there is no indication for now that the scouting trip will lead to a formal approach from them.

title: Report: Links to Barcelona defender make perfect sense
description: Alejandro Balde Liverpool links make sense amid left-back concernsLiverpool’s reported interest in Alejandro Balde fits an obvious area of squad uncertainty, but David Lynch has stressed that he can...
fullText:
Liverpool's reported interest in Alejandro Balde fits an obvious area of squad uncertainty, but David Lynch has stressed that he cannot verify the link.

Discussing the Barcelona left-back on Media Matters with David Lynch, the journalist explained why Liverpool might reasonably be assessing alternatives in the position. His comments offered context for the speculation rather than confirmation of a transfer pursuit.

"I don't know anything about that link at all in terms of how legitimate it is," Lynch said. "But it wouldn't surprise you if Liverpool were assessing their options there."

That distinction matters. An understandable recruitment idea is not evidence of negotiations, an agreed target or an impending bid.

The discussion centred on Liverpool's difficulty finding a convincing solution on the left side of defence.

Milos Kerkez's uneven start and Kostas Tsimikas's disappointing display against Fulham have left room for debate about whether the existing options provide enough consistency.

Lynch described the position as one where the manager was still searching for answers.

"Kerkez has been a bit up and down, hasn't he? It hasn't quite been a great start to the season for him."

Selecting Tsimikas offered an alternative, but the Fulham performance did little to settle the issue. Nor, in Lynch's assessment, had another straightforward solution emerged from within the squad.

"We didn't see Luke Chambers yesterday, which is interesting," he said. "So is he not quite knocking on the door in training?"

That was a question rather than a conclusion about Chambers. The broader point was that Liverpool had yet to establish an alternative that made the position feel secure.

For recruitment purposes, uncertainty of that kind naturally encourages a review of available players.

Balde's name attracts attention because he plays in a position under scrutiny. Whether he becomes a realistic Liverpool option is a separate matter, and the discussion supplied no confirmation on that front.

Lynch was clearer about the potential need than the identity of any recruit.

"I think left-back is the other position that you could quite clearly say, going into the January market, if Liverpool could do something, it'd be an interesting one to give competition there."

Competition is the important word. Liverpool's task would be to improve their options and raise the level of performance, rather than merely respond to one poor match.

Any arrival could also depend on movement elsewhere in the squad.

"Of course, it will probably require an exit for Tsimikas or whatever," Lynch added. "But let's see how that one progresses."

He did not present such an exit as agreed or inevitable. It was an acknowledgement that recruitment decisions involve existing players, available places and the balance of the group.

Liverpool also have time for the picture to change before making any decision.

Lynch was critical of Tsimikas's performance against Fulham, but recognised that it should not be treated as the only evidence available.

"Maybe he can improve on that," he said. "Maybe he'll get minutes elsewhere and absolutely rectify it, because he was very good when he came on against Atletico."

That qualification prevents the discussion becoming unnecessarily absolute. A player can struggle in one appearance and still offer useful contributions in another.

For now, the Balde links are best understood as a plausible response to Liverpool's left-back concerns. Lynch's analysis supports the logic of reviewing that position, while leaving the reported target firmly in the category of unverified speculation.

title: Arch Manning’s Apology Wins Over Holly Rowe After Viral AI Video Controversy
description: Arch Manning‘s second season as Texas’s starting quarterback was already drawing scrutiny after a rocky first year that saw him struggle early before finishing strong. That is what happened when Manning called an AI-generated video of Steve […] The post Arch Manning’s Apology Wins Over Holly Rowe After Viral AI Video Controversy appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Arch Manning's second season as Texas's starting quarterback was already drawing scrutiny after a rocky first year that saw him struggle early before finishing strong. The last thing he needed heading into 2026 was a controversy of his own making off the field.

That is what happened when Manning called an AI-generated video of Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN reporter Holly Rowe "hilarious", forcing him to issue a public apology and have a private conversation with Rowe before the Longhorns could move on. Rowe has now responded to his apology.

Manning apologized after calling an AI-generated video of Steve Sarkisian slapping Holly Rowe "hilarious" during a media session. The video followed an awkward exchange after Texas completed its comeback win over Ohio State. Manning wrote that his comment was hurtful and said he would be more thoughtful in the future.

Rowe accepted the apology after speaking with Manning privately. She said, "Thank you Arch, I appreciate our conversation about this – which will remain private. Apology accepted. We move forward with respect and kindness for one another."

The response ended the public dispute without dismissing why the reaction caused concern. Rowe has known Manning since 2017, when she met him at a Clemson practice as a 12-year-old.

That relationship gave her decision to accept the apology meaning, but it did not change the fact that Manning had laughed at a fake video showing physical violence against a real reporter who covers his program.

Manning finished last season with 3,163 passing yards, 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions, with 19 of his 36 total touchdowns coming in the final six games. Sarkisian called him a dangerous player heading into 2026 precisely because of how much he grew through adversity. That growth now has to extend beyond the field.

In his apology to Rowe, Manning had expressed remorse at his words and vowed to do better in the future.

"In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an Al video," Manning wrote. "There is nothing funny about it. It's easy to say I didn't mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that."

"I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments. I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward."

The UTSA game is Texas's first chance to put the episode behind them. Manning responded to criticism last year by going back to work and finishing the season as one of the conference's better quarterbacks. Doing the same here means treating reporters with the same professionalism Sarkisian's program demands everywhere else.

fullText:
Raptors news: Fans left baffled by video of Kawhi Leonard in studio with Chinese rapper after Clippers drama appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

After all the drama surrounding Kawhi Leonard and the Los Angeles Clippers, the recently acquired Toronto Raptors star was in the studio with a Chinese rapper, which baffled some fans.

Top Barry posted a video of himself with Leonard in the studio on Friday, Sep. 4, a couple of days after the NBA punished Steve Ballmer and the Clippers for circumventing the salary cap with Leonard.

The video was making the rounds again on Tuesday, Sep. 15, 2026, on X, formerly Twitter. Fans were divided, to say the least. One liked the last bar of the rap, calling it "tough," but another said, "I'm reading words that have never been put together before."

Someone else was extremely blunt in their take, saying, "This is worse than being paid under the table." Another fan joked, "I didn't even think bro listened to music!"

After the investigation of Ballmer and the Clippers, the Raptors' trade for Leonard, bringing him back to Toronto after he won a championship during the 2018-19 season with them, was made official.

The trade was initially finalized in June 2026 before free agency officially opened. The Clippers were to receive Brandon Ingram, Grade Dick, two first-round NBA Draft picks, two second-round picks, and a future pick swap in return.

The NBA's investigation of the Clippers' alleged salary cap circumvention put a pin in the trade. After a couple of months, it was finally made official.

Leonard previously spent one season with the Raptors after starting his career with the San Antonio Spurs. He then signed with the Clippers in free agency in 2019, remaining there until 2026.

Throughout his career, Leonard has won two championships and was named NBA Finals MVP of both series. He has also made seven All-Star teams and seven All-NBA teams (three First Team and four Second Team).

title: Did you know?
description: Rangers make the short trip across the city on Sunday aiming to achieve a derby feat they have accomplished only twice before in their history.  Having beaten Celtic 3-0 last weekend in the League Cup quarters, Rangers are now targeting back-to-back derby wins in successive games.  On only two occasions have Rangers faced their Old Firm rivals twice in a row in all competitions and won both.
fullText:
Rangers make the short trip across the city on Sunday aiming to achieve a derby feat they have accomplished only twice before in their history.

Having beaten Celtic 3-0 last weekend in the League Cup quarters, Rangers are now targeting back-to-back derby wins in successive games.

It will be be no easy task though - as history shows.

On only two occasions have Rangers faced their Old Firm rivals twice in a row in all competitions and won both.

The first came way back in September 1960 under Scot Symon as Rangers followed up a 2-1 Parkhead win in the League Cup with a 5-1 league trouncing at the same venue.

There was a 38-year wait before it happened again. Walter Smith was the manager as Rangers defeated Celtic 2-1 in the Scottish Cup semis at Celtic Park in April 1998 then racked up a 2-0 derby win at Ibrox the following weekend.

Now, a further 28 years later, can Derek McInnes and his side repeat the feat?

title: What We Learned About College Football in Week Two
description: Texas Slays A Goliath The Longhorns have beaten nearly perfect the last few seasons outside of two behemoths – Georgia and Ohio State. They finally were able to slay one of their giants with a thrilling 24-23 comeback victory over the Buckeyes. It did not come easy at all, as Texas found itself behind 23-3 […]
fullText:
The Longhorns have beaten nearly perfect the last few seasons outside of two behemoths – Georgia and Ohio State. They finally were able to slay one of their giants with a thrilling 24-23 comeback victory over the Buckeyes. It did not come easy at all, as Texas found itself behind 23-3 in the fourth quarter. But Arch Manning caught fire just in time, as the Ohio State offense suddenly became stagnant, finding it hard to move the ball unless it was in Jeremiah Smith's hands. Texas has a brutal schedule the rest of the way, but this is the kind of game that will make them believe they should beat whoever lines across the field from them on any given week.

Penn State opened 2025 ranked #2 thanks to a loaded roster and an experienced quarterback. Oregon found itself in the same spot for the same reasons in 2026. They also are off to a disastrous start that could spell doom for a season with major expectations. Despite having nearly all of its key players back on both sides of the ball, the Ducks look like a completely different team. The offense has been inconsistent at best, while the defense has found trouble getting off the field against Boise State and Oklahoma State. The loss in Stillwater was a complete stunner, as Oklahoma State had lost its last 12 games to FBS programs before upsetting #6 Oregon. The Ducks have their work cut out to fix so many early-season issues, especially with a trip to red-hot USC coming up in two weeks.

The Red Raiders were the runaway favorites to win the Big 12 heading into the season. Their performance against Oregon State on Saturday suggests the race may be more open than we thought. Not only did Texas Tech find itself down in the fourth quarter, they also allowed nearly 500 yards and over 400 passing yards. They lost some serious talent to the NFL in 2025, including the #2 overall pick in pass rusher David Bailey. While the Red Raiders may have a massive payroll, the new additions from a highly-rated portal class may not connect this time around.

I'm still not sure what to take from Michigan's win over Oklahoma. The Wolverines took a giant step after a disastrous performance against Western Michigan in week one. However, Oklahoma and Michigan seem to be mirrored versions of each other. Both have stingy defenses that make it difficult for anyone to find yards, while you just cross your fingers and hope the offense can come up with a big play here and there without the ability to move the ball consistently. It also seems clear that Michigan will need to rely on Bryce Underwood running the ball regularly to have any chance on offense. He had 16 rushing attempts against the Sooners, which will likely be a regular trend as long as he is under center. Is that a winning formula to get through the entirety of the Big Ten schedule?

Penn State wasn't the only team who did not look as impressive in week two. Iowa needed to overcome a 10-0 deficit and a last-second field goal to get past Iowa State. Washington struggled against Utah State in a 16-14 victory. Others weren't as fortunate. Minnesota was soundly defeated by Mississippi State at home. Purdue lost in triple overtime to Wake Forest. And Rutgers fell to 0-2 after a loss to Boston College. It was not a banner day for the Big Ten, especially with Ohio State and Oregon getting tripped up.

title: Drew Brees Reveals ‘No Pop’ Truth Behind Sean Payton’s Failed Attempt to Replace Injured Bo Nix
description: Bo Nix fractured his ankle on the second-to-last play of Denver’s divisional round win over the Buffalo Bills last January, right before the Broncos kicked the field goal that sent them to the AFC Championship. Within hours, the franchise was scrambling to find a starting quarterback to face the New England Patriots, and the name […] The post Drew Brees Reveals ‘No Pop’ Truth Behind Sean Payton’s Failed Attempt to Replace Injured Bo Nix appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Bo Nix fractured his ankle on the second-to-last play of Denver's divisional round win over the Buffalo Bills last January, right before the Broncos kicked the field goal that sent them to the AFC Championship. Within hours, the franchise was scrambling to find a starting quarterback to face the New England Patriots, and the name that came up was Drew Brees.

The contact came the same morning Brees learned he had been selected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Rather than dismiss the idea, he went outside to throw to his son to find out if his body could still handle an NFL game.

Offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and offensive assistant Pete Carmichael made the call to Brees directly. Both had coached him during his years with Sean Payton in New Orleans, and that familiarity made the conversation possible. Brees said he knew around 20 people in the Broncos organization and was genuinely open to helping them reach the Super Bowl.

Before making any decision, Brees wanted to find out if his body could handle playing again. He worked out with his son, Callen. The session was a reality check for the former QB. He said, "I started trying to rip the ball to him. And man, this shoulder and this right wrist are so wasted. I got no pop. So for people to say like, 'Oh, I felt discomfort?' Discomfort my butt, dude. I can't throw 15 yards with any kind of pop…"

He shared that he still had strong ties to the organization, knowing around 20 people there, and viewed the opportunity as a challenge late in his football journey, but it was not to be.

Brees had retired after the 2020 season and had not played a competitive snap in five years. The workout confirmed that his arm, specifically the wrist and shoulder that had been deteriorating toward the end of his career, could not meet the demands of an AFC Championship Game.

One of the more striking details to emerge from the reporting is that Sean Payton had no idea Lombardi and Carmichael had reached out to Brees. The two assistants wanted to gauge Brees' interest before bringing it to their head coach.

Payton only found out during the offseason, and when he first heard about it he reportedly thought they were referring to 2021, when New Orleans briefly explored bringing Brees back during a quarterback injury crisis that season. Brees made clear that mentally he was ready to try.

"There's like 20 guys in that Broncos organization that I know and love," he said. "I would love nothing more than to help them win a game to get to the Super Bowl and then go win that thing. I'd love to go up against that Mike MacDonald defense. So much respect for him. I was mentally ready. The rest of my body? Ready. But right arm and right wrist? They lost it a long time ago."

There was also a separate logistical obstacle. Brees remained on the New Orleans Saints' reserve-retired list, and the NFL's deadline for a retired player to return had already passed. Even if the wrist had held up, Denver may not have had a legal path to put him on the field.

In the end, Denver handed the job to Jarrett Stidham, while Brees' brief comeback consideration remained an interesting what-if story of the Broncos' playoff run.

Brees retired after the 2020 season. In 12 games for the New Orleans Saints that year, he completed 275 of 390 passes for 2,942 yards, 24 touchdowns and six interceptions. He finished the season with a 70.5% completion rate and a 106.4 passer rating.

Brees finished his 20-year career with 287 regular-season games, 80,358 passing yards, 571 touchdowns and 243 interceptions. He also completed 67.7% of his career passes, finishing among the NFL's most productive quarterbacks.

title: ESPN reportedly makes $100 million Joe Buck decision
description: Here's the latest on Joe Buck's new deal with ESPN.
fullText:
ESPN reportedly makes $100 million Joe Buck decision originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Joe Buck is one of the most recognizable names in sports media, and he isn't going anywhere anytime soon.

The 57-year-old is set to sign a new extension to remain with ESPN for the next six years, keeping him as one of the voices of the NFL schedule. Buck is currently in his fifth year with ESPN, the final year of his deal, and is set to call the Super Bowl once again when ABC and ESPN get the game in February of 2027.

When Buck moved from Fox to ESPN, he largely pivoted his focus solely to football as he took over "Monday Night Football" with his longtime partner, Troy Aikman. As a result, "Monday Night Football" has regained prestige from decades ago, giving ABC and ESPN the ability to land a Super Bowl broadcast.

Here's the latest on Joe Buck's new deal with ESPN.

NFL HQ:Live NFL scores | Updated NFL standings | Full NFL schedule

Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reports that ESPN has signed Joe Buck to a six-year, $108 million extension that begins after this NFL season and keeps the broadcaster as the voice of "Monday Night Football" for the foreseeable future.

Buck left Fox to join ESPN in 2022, along with his partner Troy Aikman, to focus solely on "Monday Night Football" broadcasts. Buck had been with Fox from 1994 to 2021, broadcasting both NFL and MLB games, but ESPN gave him a lucrative deal to elevate its football broadcasts.

Joe Buck and ESPN have agreed on a new contract worth over $100 million to keep Buck as the voice of “Monday Night Football” into the next decade.

(via @AndrewMarchand) pic.twitter.com/QCCwceTsVf

Over the past few years, Buck has called a select number of MLB games for ESPN, but he was not a regular on those broadcasts even before the network lost "Sunday Night Baseball" to NBC. Marchand does report that ESPN president Jimmy Pitaro would like the network to get World Series broadcasts in the future, and he would like Buck to be the one to call those games, but that isn't part of this extension.

Buck's previous deal was for five years and $75 million, according to Marchand, so he gets a notable raise in his new deal. Not only will he make $3 million more per season, but Buck also gets an extra year on his new contract.

While Buck is locked up moving forward, Aikman's contract is still set to expire after the season. So, it's possible Buck has a new partner when this extension begins in 2027.

MORE: Week 1 overreactions - The Bears offense is unstoppable

ABC and ESPN are set to broadcast Super Bowl 61 in February, marking the first-ever ESPN Super Bowl and teh first ABC Super Bowl since February of 2006. Back then, Al Michaels and John Madden called the game for ABC before they moved together to NBC, similar to Buck and Aikman's move together.

Buck's extension means he will also be on the call when ABC and ESPN broadcast Super Bowl 65 in February of 2031, the next and only other Super Bowl on ABC and ESPN's schedule. Buck also called six Super Bowls while working with Fox.

title: Georgia baseball coach Wes Johnson gets another contract extension, pay increase

title: NFL Hands Down Decision on Texans’ Azeez Al-Shaair, 3 Key Stars After Bills Game Incident
description: Houston Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined $11,492 by the NFL for writing “Hind Rajab” on his eye black during the Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills. It is his second fine for an unauthorized message, after the league fined him $11,593 last January for writing “Stop The Genocide” during the playoff win over […] The post NFL Hands Down Decision on Texans’ Azeez Al-Shaair, 3 Key Stars After Bills Game Incident appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Houston Texans linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair was fined $11,492 by the NFL for writing "Hind Rajab" on his eye black during the Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills. It is his second fine for an unauthorized message, after the league fined him $11,593 last January for writing "Stop The Genocide" during the playoff win over Pittsburgh.

Hind Rajab was a five-year-old Palestinian girl killed in Gaza City in January 2024, and Al-Shaair has made clear he intends to keep using his platform regardless of the cost.

Three of his teammates were also fined as part of the same round of penalties. Al-Shaair, who is Muslim, has used his platform consistently to draw attention to the conflict, wearing "Free Palestine" cleats through the NFL's My Cause My Cleats program and hosting child amputees from Gaza at Texans games.

Al-Shaair addressed the fine directly, making clear he understood the consequences before he took the field.

"At the end of the day, it's bigger than me," Al-Shaair told Aaron Wilson. "The things that are going on make people uncomfortable, imagine how those people feel. I think that's the biggest thing. I have no affiliation, no connection to these people other than the fact that I'm a human being."

He also added, "If you have a heart and you're a human being you can see what's going on in the world and you check yourself real quick. Even when I'm walking off this field, that's the type of stuff that goes through my head that I have to check myself when I'm sitting here crying about football when there's people dying every single day. If my platform can bring even a little hope to families in Palestine, then that is what I want to use it for."

After his January fine, Al-Shaair also pushed back on the threat of being removed from the game entirely. "I never seen Stef get pulled out of a game for having eye tape with writing on it," he said, referencing Stefon Diggs.

The fine was issued under Rule 6, Section 4, Article 8 of the NFL rulebook, which bans personal messages on game day equipment unless approved in advance by the league. The NFL does not grant approval for messages related to political causes. CAIR-Houston pointed out that the league fined Al-Shaair while allowing players to wear pins supporting the Stand Up to Jewish Hate campaign led by Patriots owner Robert Kraft.

Al-Shaair's bigger issue was that officials threatened to pull him from the game during the playoff win over Pittsburgh if he kept the message on. When addressing the matter, Al-Shaair brought up Stefon Diggs by name, pointing to the fact that his former teammate had written messages on his eye tape for years without ever being pulled from a game for it.

"I was told that if I wore that in the game, I would be pulled out the game," Al-Shaair said. "That was the part that I was confused about, because I understood it was a fine, but I ain't never seen Stef get pulled out the game for having eye tape with writing on it."

Diggs, who played alongside Al-Shaair in Houston last season before signing with New England, has written personal messages on his eye tape multiple times without ever being pulled from a game. That included a tribute to his brother Trevon after Trevon suffered a torn ACL in 2023, and a "Free Chap" message during a game in October 2024 while still with the Texans. He was fined for those but never removed from the field, which is exactly the inconsistency Al-Shaair was pointing to.

title: Enow Etta reveals Michigan's mindset entering Oklahoma upset
description: Michigan defensive tackle Enow Etta says the team ignored national doubt to dominate Oklahoma with a tough mindset.
fullText:
ANN ARBOR, Mich. -- Though the one shining example of Michigan football still having something going after Week 1 was its defense, many expected it to fall apart once the Wolverines took the field against Oklahoma. After all, the Sooners were something of a mirror image of the maize and blue, but seemingly just better.

However, they play the games for a reason.

The Michigan defensive front had the Oklahoma offensive front in shambles for much of the game. And even though the first game left a lot to be desired, there wasn't a moment on Saturday when everything 'clicked' -- the team already knew what it had and what it was capable of. Because it had to know given how tough the schedule looked on paper.

"Oh, I mean, man, it started last week -- it started, I don't know, the offseason," senior defensive tackle Enow Etta said. "You look at the schedule -- I mean, people say what they want. It's not even rising to the challenge; it's just like, that's our schedule. You know what I mean? So, it's like, everybody on the list is like, we got to bring our A game. I don't think it was such things like, oh, them, there, them. No, it's just like, we're us, and we're going to bring our best every weekend. That's either enough, or it's enough. You know what I mean?

"So, I wouldn't even say there's rising to the challenge. It's just, we just got to play our game, and we know when we play our game, we're going to be the best. So, we just got to be our best, and we know our best. I mean, you know what I mean? Sky's the limit."

Of course, the Wolverines got more confidence as the game went on, but there was never a feeling like Oklahoma was ever going to be too much. There wasn't an early moment in the game that changed the team's belief, as if it didn't think it could handle the Sooners until such-and-such a play happened.

The maize and blue always had the belief it could go out and handle business, even if the national narrative said otherwise. As Etta says, the coaches instill confidence in them, going beyond a simple Week 2 nonconference matchup. And the team came off the bus ready to win.

"That was just the belief there. It's like, we just got to line up and do it," Etta said. "And then, as the game went on, it's like, OK, we're going pretty well, we're just going to keep doing what we're doing. And then, it gets to the end of the game, and it's like, shoot, I mean -- good outcome, I guess. You know what I mean?

"So, yeah, I mean, you got to step on the field, believe, and I believe. And I know a lot of the guys, Dom, John Henry, especially those two guys, they're crazy. But we all believe that. You know what I mean? It's like, you step on the field. If you don't think you should win, like -- the coaches tell us all the time, like, if you don't believe in us, stay in the hotel. You know what I mean? We'll just pick you up after the game on the bus. You know what I mean?

"So I think it's just like first snap mentality. It's like, you're not going out there, and you don't believe you're better than the guy in front of you, then you're just holding us back, you know?"

Through two games, Michigan's won by a combined eight points. But the defense has allowed just one touchdown and five field goals thus far -- to a Western Michigan team that put up 49 in Week 2 and an Oklahoma team that managed 51 in Week 1.

The Wolverines heard all of the chatter about how bad the team was after the first contest against the Broncos, and they used it as fuel to take down the then-10th-ranked Sooners. And now that they've fed a bit of that hunger, Etta insists the team is still that much more ravenous to prove what it's capable of.

"It's what we expected to do, you know what I mean?" Etta said. "Going into that game, it wasn't a surprise to all of us because that's what we were working for all week. We knew what we could do, and we kind of had our backs to the wall in terms of the whole country. So, we were like, let's show everybody what we can do. So when we went out there, I mean, it might have been a surprise to a lot of people, but we knew that was our standard. And we're going to continue to put that on tape every week."

The Oklahoma defense shut out UTEP in Week 1. The Miners are now coming to Ann Arbor, and assuredly the Michigan defense will look to do the same. Kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on BTN.

title: Nebraska and Notre Dame announce home-and-home series with games in 2032-33

Nebraska will host Notre Dame in Lincoln on Oct. 30, 2032, and the Irish will host the Cornhuskers in South Bend on Oct. 29, 2033. fullText:
Nebraska and Notre Dame have scheduled a home-and-home series with games in 2032 and 2033 in what will be the first matchups of the tradition-rich programs in more than three decades, the schools announced Wednesday.

Nebraska will host Notre Dame in Lincoln on Oct. 30, 2032, and the Irish will host the Cornhuskers in South Bend on Oct. 29, 2033.

Notre Dame ranks fourth in all-time wins with 974 and Nebraska is eighth with 933. The schools have combined for 13 national titles, with the Fighting Irish winning eight and Nebraska five.

The teams last played in 2000 and 2001 with Nebraska winning both games. Nebraska leads the all-time series 8-7-1.

"The series with Notre Dame is the type of matchup that college football fans circle on their calendars years in advance," Nebraska athletic director Troy Dannen said. "Our fans have a tremendous appreciation for the history of college football and iconic venues. We are excited to welcome Notre Dame and their fans to Lincoln in 2032, and I know our fans will travel to South Bend in full force in 2033."

title: No. 1 Texas vs. UTSA preview: Final non-conference game for Horns against a familiar foe
description: Jeff Traylor returns to Austin for the third time.
fullText:
On Saturday at 7:00 p.m. Central on SEC Network+, the No. 1 Texas Longhorns will host the UTSA Roadrunners at Darrell K. Royal Texas Memorial Stadium for the final game before SEC play begins.

UTSA heads to Austin with a 2-0 record and a starting quarterback that led the Roadrunners to 35.5 points per game a year ago. Similar to the matchup against Texas State, Texas possesses a talent advantage, but are not facing off against a radically inferior opponent — the Roadrunners have firepower and the ability to test the Longhorns.

Leading the way for the Roadrunners is head coach Jeff Traylor, a name that should be familiar for most Longhorn fans — Traylor left Gilmer High School to begin his college coaching career in Austin in 2015 as the special teams coordinator and tight ends coach before handling wide receivers as an associate head coach. He was named the Big 12 Recruiter of the Year during his tenure on the Forty Acres before stints at SMU and Arkansas with Chad Morris, another Texas high school coaching alum.

In December of 2019, Traylor accepted the head coaching role at UTSA. Just two years later, he led the way to a 12-win season that featured the first conference championship in program history.

Last season, Traylor and company tallied a 7-6 record and a win in the First Responder Bowl. The offense looks poised to put up points this season with starting quarterback Owen McCown returning while the defense has to replace many pieces from a below average unit.

"Jeff Traylor continues to do it again — they're 2-0, they're playing really good football," Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said on Monday. "We talk about the ball. These guys have created five turnovers through two games. They haven't turned the ball over once yet. They've got a veteran quarterback in Owen McCown. He's a three-year starter. He knows what he's doing. He executes their stuff. And they've got a veteran defense. I know there's new starters, but there's a lot of old players on that defense, and they play like it. So they're going to come in here ready to go."

In two previous matchups against Traylor and UTSA, Texas won 41-20 in 2022 and 56-7 in 2024.

Let's break the Roadrunners down position-by-position.

After averaging 35.5 points per game a year ago, the Roadrunners hired Rick Bowie as offensive coordinator after former OC Justin Burke accepted a role as tight ends coach at Kentucky under Will Stein, his former teammate. Traylor and Stein previously worked together underneath Charlie Strong at Texas and at UTSA.

Bowie inherited a unit that has ranked in the top 15 nationally in scoring in three of the past five years. He runs an Air Raid scheme with the motto, "Simpler, Faster, Smarter." With McCown at the helm, the Roadrunners are expected to continue putting up points with ease.

The signal caller for UTSA is McCown, a 28-game starter. The Rusk product from his own famous quarterback family battled injuries a year ago, which greatly limited his mobility from Week 2 on. Regardless, he threw for 2,995 yards and 30 touchdowns against just seven interceptions while completing 67.6 percent of his passes. He has carried that efficiency into 2026, completing 72.5 percent of his passes for 489 yards and four touchdowns without an interception through two games.

McCown is more than a pocket passer — his mobility can break a defense while his experience makes him the natural leader of the offense. Last week, he led an 82-yard touchdown drive in a comeback win against Texas State.

The PLAY that saved the game today for @UTSAFTBL Owen McCown was not gonna be denied. Fourth down conversion. #BirdsUp pic.twitter.com/QTvq3Jjp7u

If the Longhorn defense can force McCown into obvious passing situations and maintain rush lane integrity, it could make life much more difficult for the Roadrunner offense.

The leading rusher from a year ago departed for NFL, which gives full rein to redshirt sophomore Will Henderson. From Traylor's hometown of Gilmer, Henderson is considered one of the fastest players in college football by his head coach after putting up impressive numbers a year ago as RB2 — 866 yards and six touchdowns while averaging 6.9 yards per carry.

UTSA has a future star in freshman running back Will Henderson III. Look at the speed he’s bringing to the First Responder Bowl. 

And the blocking, especially from WR DJ Allen Jr., is beautiful pic.twitter.com/WGpgYq4Skb

So far this season, Henderson has already proven to be effective, accumulating 181 yards on 23 carriers and a touchdown. The 5'10, 195-pounder's high-end speed makes him a home-run threat on any play.

Behind Henderson are A'Marion Peterson and Brandon High Jr. Peterson is another returning back poised to put up impressive numbers with more carries. This season, he's turned 10 carries into 100 yards and two touchdowns, including a 53-yard scamper. Meanwhile, High has turned in a steady 5.8 yards per carry this season over 16 carries, including the game-winning touchdown last week with 14 seconds left.

BRANDON HIGH JR. RUNS IN THE GAME-WINNING TOUCHDOWN FOR UTSA!!! pic.twitter.com/Lmy5v54gNj

Together, this trio forms a room with depth and speed. Each player can turn a small gap into a chunk play thanks to elusive speed.

McCown has plenty of options with at wide receiver. Through two games, McCown has spread the ball around to three primary targets — DJ Allen, Mekhi Anderson, and AJ Wilson. David Amador is another Roadrunner that will see snaps at wideout. Wilson and Amador combined for 76 catches for 971 yards and eight touchdowns last year while Allen and Anderson have burst on to the scene this season.

As the three leading pass catchers, Allen, Anderson, and Wilson have hauled in 31 passes for 390 yards and three touchdowns. Allen possesses the speed to threaten defenses, but has also shown the ability to create after the catch, giving McCown another explosive option. The TCU transfer had just 20 catches for 189 yards last season, but appears poised for a much larger role in UTSA's new offense.

Together, the trio can blow the top off of a defense or make possession extending catches. This group is capable of winning in different ways and will test the secondary at all three levels.

The tight end room came into the season needing to replace their top three tight ends. To ease the transition into Bowie's system, Traylor relied on the portal — Miles Campbell was brought in from Florida A&M as a four-star recruit while Brandon Young Jr. arrived from North Texas.

So far, the UTSA offense has rotated bodies at the tight end spot. Young provides size at 6'7, 240 pounds, while Campbell adds pass-catching reliability after catching 22 passes for 308 yards and a touchdown last year.

The offensive line returns a good number of players from a year ago, but injuries have derailed the preseason plans for this group. Ben Dios, a 6'5, 315-pound redshirt senior starts at left guard while Darrell Jones, a 6'4 320-pound senior handles the right guard spot. Each of these players is experienced and versatile. At center is redshirt senior Luke Lapeze. The 6'5, 320-pound lineman started 11 games in 2023 before injuries derailed the previous two years.

UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor said yesterday that the Roadrunners are banged up at offensive tackle.

“It’s a work in process. We will get better, but we haven’t been real good yet at (offensive tackle).”

Former Longhorn Jaylen Garth has seen a lot of time at RT. #HookEm

The two tackle spots are fluid thanks to injury and overall skill level. Against Texas State last week, the Roadrunners listed co-starters at both tackle spots. Sixth-year Jaylen Garth is a seasoned veteran who started his career at Texas as a highly-heralded recruit. After a stint at Houston, Garth landed in San Antonio. He started nine games in 2024 before an injury derailed his 2025 season. He was granted a medical redshirt and has seen time at tackle this year. He'll certainly be amped to play his former team come Saturday.

The Roadrunner defense is headed by Jess Loepp, who enters his sixth season in the role. Loepp led a unit that dominated during wins and underperformed greatly in losses a year ago. The defense allowed 18 points per game in seven wins last year compared to 41.5 in losses last season, a huge discrepancy. Allowing 28.8 points per game placed UTSA 91st nationally in that category.

"Statistics don't look good, but we probably started out the year at 138, and we finally climbed up to 90. When you when you replace your one-deep and two-deep, that's pretty staggering," Traylor told Horns247.

With nearly 65 percent of defensive production no longer on the roster, Loepp is responsible for improving his unit with a variety of new players. As the defense continues to nail down its two-deep, expectations are low, though Texas State scored only 26 points a week ago.

Up front, the Roadrunners utilize an odd front. At nose is senior Jameian Buxton. At 6'2, 325 pounds, Buxton is big and experienced. He's started 36 games over the last three seasons and is one of the most reliable UTSA defenders.

Where will the nation's top uncommitted defensive tackles land? @adamgorney makes his predictions, including projecting four-star Jameian Buxton to land at LSU: https://t.co/VNRLv7dQRs pic.twitter.com/BFNmjG2zoa

At one end position is redshirt senior Tai Leonard, who returns after starting nine games last season, and has recorded two quarterback hits thus far. Counterpart is redshirt senior Jeremiah Bailey brings a nice frame at 6'3, 285 pounds and is expected to make plays.

Bailey transferred from Eastern Kentucky where he recorded 105 total tackles, 14 tackles for loss, six sacks, two fumble recoveries, a pair of pass breakups, and one fumble recovery in 38 career games.

As the game wore on against Texas State, the UTSA defensive lined relied heavily on their starters rather than tapping into their depth, a possible sign of the talent drop off among players.

Against Texas, I'd expect a heavier rotation of bodies though the Longhorns should still be able to impose their will against the starting three up front.

The linebacker room was hurt by two key departures, including 93 tackles from Shad Banks. This group will have some new faces present to recoup that lost production.

The best pass rusher for the Roadrunners is redshirt junior Camron Cooper. At 6'2, 245 pounds, Cooper returns from injury with high expectations, but so far, the pass rush for the entire team has been minimal with the defense recording just one sack thus far. I'd expect a heavy dose of blitz on Saturday as UTSA tries to conjure up pressure.

At the JACK role is Owen Pewee. Pewee spent the previous two seasons at the money backer role on the outside and thrived. The 6'3, 220-pound senior had recorded 106 career tackles, 17 tackles for loss, three sacks and three interceptions entering into the season. He's moving back inside and is strong enough to maneuver around linemen and athletic enough to drop back in coverage. Pewee starred in high school at Cypress Park with former LSU linebacker Harold Perkins.

The MIKE spot is held by redshirt senior Brandon Tucker. Tucker led the way against Texas State with 13 tackles and is currently leading the team with 18 on the year.

Redshirt senior Darion White has been a steady presence inside while redshirt junior James Walley Jr. recorded the lone sack on the season.

There are a lot of moving parts at the linebacker spot. With new faces, players in different positions, and a deep room, there will likely be a deep rotation on Saturday.

The safety position was uncertain heading into the season after a spring injury to junior Joel Rogers required surgery. Rogers is third on the team in tackles despite not starting against Texas State and brings physicality to the group.

The two starters last week were senior Cameron Upshaw and junior Elijah Newell. Newell is a bit undersized while Upshaw is simply unproven. The Texas wideout group should be able to exploit the physical and mental advantages his has over the two safeties.

The corner group is possibly the deepest and most talented of any defensive position. Twin brothers Ahamad and Asaad Chapman are talented athletes with a track record of quality play, though Asaad's was at the JUCO level.

In addition, RJ Lester is a lanky cover guy at 6'3, 190 pounds. He transferred from Oklahoma State and provides great size for the secondary.

This group is a strength of the team, but will ultimately be challenged greatly by the Texas wideouts.

Handling kicking duties is senior Michael Petro, who connected on 17-of-20 (85 percent) of his field goals last season with a long of 45 yards. Petro is 2-of-3 (66.6 percent) this season. He doesn't possesses elite leg strength, as evidenced by no attempts of 50-plus yards in his career.

Junior Caile Hogan will punt on Saturday. Hogan is an Aussie punter who was rather effective last year. He was recognized as the second-team All-AAC punter last year and put up the second-best punting average in UTSA history last year at 45.7 yards per punt. He's a special teams weapon.

Amador returns punts, averaging 7.0 yards per return over three attempts.

Anderson and High will be back deep for kickoffs. Anderson is the primary returner and has a season long of 27 yards.

Texas should be able to attack UTSA both on the ground and through the air, while defensively the Longhorns need to limit McCown's ability to extend plays and hit explosive passes. I anticipate UTSA playing aggressively and testing Texas early, though most expect the outcome of this game to sway mightily toward the Longhorns.

Texas is a 30.5-point favorite, according to FanDuel.

title: Red Sox Magic Number: When Will They Clinch Postseason Spot?
description: The Boston Red Sox's magic number sits at five
fullText:
The Boston Red Sox's loss to the Texas Rangers on Tuesday night shook up the American League wild card race.

The Red Sox's loss did not change their standing, but it helped push the Rangers past the Toronto Blue Jays in the standings. The Rangers are now the first team out of the postseason, trailing the Cleveland Guardians by 1 1/2 games. The Blue Jays are now 2 games out of a postseason spot. With the Rangers and Blue Jays swapping spots, the Red Sox's magic number did not change.

The Boston Red Sox can simply win five games in the final 11 games of the year and be guaranteed to be playing baseball in October. However, they would prefer to punch their ticket well before that. Luckily for the Red Sox, they can help themselves out a little extra this week.

Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand-new baseball lifestyle brand!

The Red Sox need any combination of wins and losses by the first team out of the postseason to equal five. Right now, that team could be the Rangers, Blue Jays or Baltimore Orioles. Red Sox fans should be rooting against all three of those teams the rest of the way.

Even though winning the division is not mathematically impossible, it is extremely unlikely. The Red Sox trail by 9 1/2 games with 11 games left to play. They are essentially locked in as the No. 5 seed in the American League postseason.

That means they will play the top wild card team, which, at the moment, is the New York Yankees. The Red Sox would have to travel to the Bronx for that best-of-three series, but there's a slight chance that they won't face the Yankees.

The Yankees trail the Tampa Bay Rays by 3 1/2 games in the American League East, and will play a four-game series against the Rays starting next Tuesday. If the Yankees can win the division, the Red Sox would head to Tropicana Field for a wild card series against the Rays.

title: Bijan Robinson did something Week 1 no NFL player has in 40 years
description: Falcons RB almost beats 1986 record by Eric Dickerson
fullText:
Perhaps the most frustrating thing about the Atlanta Falcons' ongoing dumpster fire at quarterback is that it's wasting the prime years of some very special skill players - especially fourth-year stud Bijan Robinson.

Atlanta's superstar running back just passed Devonta Freeman on the franchise's all-time rushing list, and at the same time Robinson was so dominant in Week 1 that he came close to beating a fiendish 40-year NFL record set by Rams legend Eric Dickerson. Kevin Patra at NFL.com has the details.

"Bijan Robinson generated 173 scrimmage yards, including 90 receiving yards, most among all RBs through Sunday. Robinson accounted for 65.8% of the Falcons' yards from scrimmage in Week 1, the highest share by any player in a team's season opener since Rams RB Eric Dickerson (66.6%) in 1986."

Dickerson went on to make six Pro Bowl teams, earn five first-team All-Pro honors and eventually made the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Along the way, Dickerson won multiple Offensive Player of the Year awards and made the Hall of Fame all 80's team. He appeared in seven career playoff games, averaging over 100 yards in those contests and scoring three touchdowns.

The only thing missing from Dickerson's resume was a Super Bowl win - and right now it looks like Bijan Robinson's career path is on a similar trajectory. Somebody needs to find the final piece of the puzzle and give Robinson, Drake London and the rest of the gang a legitimate chance to win a ring.
