title: These Are the Best Tablets to Gift in 2026
description: There's an iPad or an Android tablet out there for everyone.
fullText:
If someone on your gift list wants a new tablet, it can be a daunting challenge. Like smartphones, taste in tablets is highly dependent on platform preference. If the person you're buying for has an iPhone, they may struggle with an Android tablet. Likewise, Android users may be looking for a tablet that runs the same OS as their phones, and an iPad won't help them there. Still yet, some people like to mix and match: some prefer an Android smartphone, but an iPad for tablet use. As such, I highly recommend asking your recipient what device they're looking for.

But even if you don't know the exact tablet model your friend or family member wants, you can still pick up a great gift. As long as you know whether they'd prefer an iPad or an Android tablet, and whether they have a casual interest in this device, or are a power user.

Apple sells a lot of iPads, at a variety of sizes and price points. Whether you walk into a retail store or browse Apple's online marketplace, you may find yourself overwhelmed by the options. But unless your giftee has any specific requirements beyond "iPad," "iPad" is what you should buy.

At the risk of adding to the confusion, "iPad" is the official name for Apple's base model tablet. Some call it the 11th generation iPad, others call it the iPad A16, after the chip that powers the device. Either way, it is by far the best iPad for most people looking for an Apple tablet, whether your giftee is a student or a casual user. That's because it does almost everything you'd expect an iPad to do, all at a very reasonable price—especially when compared to Apple's other tablets.

This iPad has an 11-inch IPS display with a resolution of 2360 x 1640. It can reach 500 nits of brightness, which, while not the brightest screen Apple makes, should be enough for most use cases. It doesn't have some of the perks of some of Apple's other displays, like 120Hz refresh rate, P3 color gamut, or OLED, but for most people and most use cases, this screen will work just fine.

As mentioned above, this iPad is running Apple's A16 chip, the same Apple used for its iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That means you're getting a slower chip than in Apple's more expensive tablets, but there's more to it than that. iPadOS isn't macOS: This operating system requires far less horsepower to run, especially for lighter tasks like email, web browsing, and media consumption. This iPad isn't the choice for users who want to primarily design 3D graphics, edit 4K video, or play AAA games, but it will run just about most other tasks and apps just fine.

iPads aren't known for their cameras, but they can be decent. The same is true here: You get a 12MP camera on the back that supports 4K video. But, more importantly, there's a 12MP selfie camera that supports Center Stage. This automatically keeps you centered in the frame, which makes it easier to take FaceTime calls while moving around—say, if you're cooking. The iPad comes with plenty of other modern features, like a USB-C port, Wi-Fi 6 and 5G support. Of course, it supports the Apple Pencil, but make sure you buy the correct model. (Apple Pencil USB-C). It also supports Apple's Magic Keyboard, but you can find third-party alternatives as well.

This iPad starts at a great price, but like many of the options on this list, you're only getting 128GB of storage for it. That can be usable, but if your giftee is the type to keep a lot of files on their devices, you may want to opt for a higher-storage version. Luckily, this tablet is often on sale, so you might find the 256GB or 512GB options at a discount.

Apple's base model iPad is excellent, but I can't say it's perfect. Apple makes iPads with better displays, far more powerful processors, and support for better accessories. The iPad is the best tablet for most people, but if you're buying a tablet specifically for a power user, I'd point you towards the iPad Pro.

The Pro comes in two sizes: 11-inch and 13-inch. Either way, you're getting Apple's "Ultra Retina XDR display," with a 120Hz refresh rate and P3 color gamut. These are OLED displays, which means high contrast, deep blacks, and no visible backlight in dark scenes. These displays are brighter, too, reaching 1000 nits in SDR and 1600 nits when viewing HDR content.

While iPadOS is just about the same on the iPad Pro as it is on the iPad (A16), the hardware between these two devices couldn't be more different. The current iPad Pros run Apple's M5 chip, the same processors found in Apple's Macs. The entry-model Pros come with a nine-core CPU and 10-core GPU with 12GB of memory. Make no mistake: These really are touchscreen computers. Unfortunately for that hardware, it's running iPadOS, so for most tasks, you're not going to notice a wild difference between the iPad Pro and iPad—perhaps unless you start running multiple apps on-screen at once. Where you will notice a difference, however, is with AI: Apple's iPad can't run Apple Intelligence, so if your recipient is interested in the company's suite of AI features, the Pro has the iPad beat.

Again, you don't buy an iPad for the camera, and, like the iPad, the Pro comes with a 12MP rear camera. Unlike the iPad, however, the Pro supports ProRes video, a professional video codec. That likely isn't an important consideration, however, save for a very small niche that may be interested in recording and editing ProRes video entirely on their iPad. It also has a 12MP Center Stage camera, and a TrueDepth camera system like on the iPhone, as this iPad supports Face ID.

The iPad Pro supports Apple Pencil Pro, the company's newer stylus accessory, as well as the Magic Keyboard, which turns the Pro into a sort of laptop. (In both function and price.) It supports 5G, as well as Wi-Fi 7, which could provide faster speeds than the base iPad. At the end of the day, the iPad Pro is the optional upgrade here: It costs far more than the iPad (A16), so it's really the choice for a recipient who wants the most power possible in their Apple tablet.

Ideally, this recommendation would be something in line with the iPad (A16). And typically, Samsung's "FE" tablet might not fit the bill, since its MSRP is considerably higher than Apple's budget iPad. But the Tab S10 FE often goes on sale, as it is at the time of writing. And at a discount, it's a fantastic choice for most people looking for an Android tablet.

The S10 FE comes with the Exynos 1580 running Android 15. The base model comes with 8GB of RAM, but upgrade to the 256GB option, and you get 12GB of RAM. According to Geekbench, the tablet scores a 1367 in single-core performance, and 3939 in multi-core performance. By comparison, Apple's iPad (A16) scores a 2572 in single-core and 5828 in multi-core. Apple has the advantage here, since it develops both the hardware and software for its tablets, but the S10 FE isn't the fastest tablet by any measure. Still, it's enough power to run the tasks you need on Android.

Like Apple's best iPad for most people, the S10 FE comes with a 10.9-inch IPS LCD. This one's a bit faster than Apple's display, though—whereas the iPad has a 60Hz display, the S10 FE has a 90Hz screen, which means swiping around the system will seem a bit smoother with a direct comparison. While you can't expect the inky blacks of an OLED display, this LCD has a resolution 1440 x 2304, which should be quite sharp. The S10 FE comes with one 13MP rear camera, and a 12MP front-facing camera. It supports Wi-Fi 6e, Bluetooth 5.3, and USB-C (2.0).

This is not the tablet to get someone who is looking to run demanding apps or playing AAA games. However, if your giftee just needs an Android tablet for watching shows and movies, messaging, and getting lightweight work done, this is one of the best values in the Android tablet market—particularly when it's on sale. Also like its Galaxy S series, Samsung has pledged seven years of software support for the Galaxy Tab series, so you can expect to see updates for the S10 FE until 2032.

The Galaxy Tab S11 line is perhaps the closest equivalent to the iPad Pro line in the Android tablet space. It comes in two variants: The S11, which has an 11-inch display, and the S11 Ultra, which has a 14.6-inch display. Either way, you're getting a tablet with a 120Hz refresh rate, HDR10+ support, and 1000 nits of typical brightness (with 1600 nits during HDR content). Like the iPad Pro, these displays are also OLED, which means your content will have better contrast and deeper blacks.

These tablets are running Mediatek Dimensity 9400+ chips built on 3nm tech. The base models for both come with 12GB of RAM, but if you get the 1TB Ultra, you'll get 16GB of RAM (though that starts to get into wildly expensive territory for a tablet). Your giftee should have more than enough power to run Android 16 on this hardware, as well as most any task they set their tablet to. CNET notes that the S11 tablets run about 25% faster than the previous generation, and that the tablet outperforms just about all others in most notable categories—minus CPU, in which the S11 comes second to the OnePlus Pad 3.

The S11 has two rear cameras: a 13MP main camera, and an 8MP ultrawide. While these are tablet cameras, reviews suggest they are perfectly usable, and the inclusion of an ultrawide could prove useful. The S11 is reasonably durable, especially against debris and spills, as the tablet has an IP68 rating against dust and water.

This is a true tablet, not a touchscreen PC, but Samsung does have some options for users who are looking for a more traditional experience. As with its Galaxy S series, the Tab S11 comes with DeX, which lets you connect the tablet to a monitor with a PC-like setup. This only works when connected to an external display, but you can, of course, replicate a laptop experience by connecting the S11 to a keyboard accessory.

Some tablets are "small," especially when compared to laptops, but few are tiny. If your recipient is looking for something that's essentially a big smartphone, your best bet is the iPad mini. The mini really is mini: Apple outfitted this model with an 8.3-inch IPS display, with a maximum brightness of 500 nits. It has a resolution of 1488 x 2266, with the same P3 color gamut as Apple's more premium tablets.

In addition, this iPad comes with Apple's A17 Pro chip, the same chip the company uses for the iPhone 15 Pro. That gives you a good balance between the Mac-level chips you find in the Pro iPads, and the older A16 found in the base iPad. What's more, this chip supports Apple Intelligence, so if you're interested in Apple's first-party AI features, the mini can run them. (Though expect some of the more demanding features, like Siri voice customization, to be inaccessible.)

The iPad mini has a similar 12MP rear camera to the base iPad, as well as 12MP Center Stage camera. However, one small knock here is that Apple still has the front camera placed in "portrait" orientation, meaning the camera is off to the side when holding the iPad sideways. Both the iPad (A16) and iPad Pro now place the camera in landscape, mimicking a laptop orientation. Not a deal breaker by any means, but something to note.

In many other respects, this is a modern iPad. It has a USB-C port, Wi-Fi 6E and 5G support, and support for Apple Pencil Pro. Apple doesn't make a keyboard accessory for the mini like it does its other iPads, but you can find third-party options online.

title: English village votes to leave the UK over migrant housing plan
description: A tiny English village has voted to leave the United Kingdom as a symbolic protest against government plans to house up to 1,200 asylum seekers on a nearby military base.  Residents of Piddington, whi...
fullText:
LONDON (AP) — A tiny English village has voted to leave the United Kingdom as a symbolic protest against government plans to house up to 1,200 asylum seekers on a nearby military base.

Residents of Piddington, which has a population of about 350, voted overwhelmingly for secession in the non-binding referendum. The results announced on Wednesday showed 285 votes in favor of breaking away, with 26 villagers voting against.

"We have given an absolute message, not just to the region, not just to the country, but to the world," said the parish chairman, Tim McNally. He said the district will henceforth be known as "the Principality of Piddington."

The attention-grabbing vote was called to oppose plans to turn the former Ministry of Defense Bicester base — which is about half a mile (0.8 kilometers) from the village — into housing for male migrants. The government says the site is "designed to be largely self‑sufficient to minimize any impact on the local community."

Residents in the Oxfordshire village have raised fears about safety, crime and the effect on house prices in the affluent area, 50 miles (80 kilometers) northwest of London.

Supporters called the declaration of independence a victory for people power and local democracy. Some media coverage compared the gesture to the classic 1949 Ealing comedy film "Passport to Pimlico," in which a London neighborhood breaks away from Britain.

Others said the campaign had a darker side and stirred up fear of newcomers. Some backers of the Piddington referendum compared their fight against the asylum accommodation to the 1940 Battle of Britain against Nazi Germany.

Villager Herbert Owen, 76, said after voting on Tuesday that the independence referendum "isn't just about Piddington," adding: "It means everything our grandparents, our parents fought for. Today is the Battle of Britain."

Comparing unauthorized immigration to an invasion has become increasingly common among politicians including Nigel Farage of Reform UK, and far-right groups that have been active in organizing and attending anti-immigrant protests.

The U.K. has seen a wave of anti-immigrant demonstrations since riots erupted two years ago after a teenager killed three young girls during a dance class near Liverpool. The U.K.-born attacker had been wrongly identified on social media as a Muslim asylum seeker.

Protesters clashed with police last year outside hotels housing asylum seekers in London and several other cities.

In June, masked men in Northern Ireland set fire to several homes in Belfast they believed to house immigrants after a Sudanese man was arrested over a stabbing.

Earlier this month, masked demonstrators blocked the port of Dover, in southeast England, and tried to stop a boatload of migrants being taken ashore in Portsmouth on the country's south coast.

The center-left Labour Party government of Prime Minister Andy Burnham says it is making progress in processing asylum claims more quickly, so that migrants spend less time in state-sponsored accommodation, and stopping people crossing the English Channel in inflatable dinghies.

More than 41,000 people made the hazardous journey in 2025, but the number so far this year is down by more than 40% from the same period last year.

The government has also pledged to move migrants from hotels and rooming houses — often in poorer neighborhoods — into more suitable accommodation.

"I understand the strength of feeling," Burnham said on Wednesday. "I will look at the issues being raised by the community and in the referendum, but we have to ensure that we have a fair plan" that spreads the burden of accommodating new arrivals across the country.

Refugee groups said military barracks aren't the right place to house asylum seekers, but cautioned that migrants should not be made scapegoats.

"For people who have fled war and violence and come to the U.K. to be safe, being accommodated in such remote and unsettling environments only exacerbates their sense of insecurity," said Jon Featonby, chief policy analyst at the Refugee Council.

"And as we've seen from other sites, they've undermined social cohesion."

title: Walmart heirs Olivia and Tom Walton are committing $100 million to America’s maternal death crisis—and betting states and donors will pour in more
description: The couple is treating it as seed money, hoping states and other donors will multiply it to tackle the maternal mortality crisis.
fullText:
The U.S. has one of the highest maternal mortality rates among wealthy nations, research shows, so heirs of the multibillion Walmart fortune are working to drastically lower it.

On Thursday, Healthy Moms, Healthy Babies America (HMHBA) announced an initial $100 million, five-year commitment from Olivia and Tom Walton to accelerate efforts to cut maternal deaths in half across the U.S. However, the investment will fund state-matching grants, partnerships, and infrastructure, so HMHBA will use the multimillion-dollar gift as a springboard to drive more public and private capital.

Olivia Walton founded HMHBA, an independent 501c3, in May to cut maternal mortality rates in half over the next five years. She made the mission personal.

"It was more dangerous for me to give birth to my children than it was for my mother to give birth to me in the 1980s," she said in a statement. "That is inexcusable—and it is fixable."

She argues the solutions to maternal mortality already exist; it's just a matter of getting resources to more mothers. This includes getting them into care earlier, extending postpartum support beyond a six-week checkup, and building care around what families actually need.

"Nearly 90 percent of maternal deaths are preventable," Walton continued. "We know what works, and states across the country are already proving it."

Even after a decline in 2023, the U.S. maternal mortality rate sat at nearly 19 deaths per 100,000 live births, which is higher than most other high-income countries. That year, 669 women died of maternal causes, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The risk isn't evenly spread. For Black women, the rate was 50.3 deaths per 100,000 live births, more than three times the rate for white women. Two-thirds of maternal deaths happen in the year after birth, HMHBA notes, and 40% of mothers don't receive follow-up care. Rural mothers also face worse odds as hospitals keep closing obstetric units.

"The U.S. spends more money for worse outcomes on maternal health. Far more than any other country in the entire world," HMHBA Executive Director Robin Reck said in a statement. "Eighty-seven percent of these deaths are preventable, and 65% of them happen after the baby is born. That is unacceptable. And it is un-American."

Maternal mortality is also costly. Poor health outcomes in 2020 cost the U.S. economy an estimated $165 billion, according to a Heartland Forward study. So preventing just half of those avoidable outcomes would save nearly $80 billion per year. For example, a healthy, full-term delivery costs about $6,400, while an extreme preterm birth can cost $238,000. March of Dimes also found first-year medical costs run roughly four times higher for preterm infants than for full-term ones.

Tom Walton is the grandson of Walmart founder Sam Walton, and the family's roughly 44% stake in the No. 2 Fortune 500 company is worth about $440 billion, Fortune's former senior reporter Jessica Matthews reported earlier this year.

The collective scale of the family's philanthropy also puts them in the same boat as legendary American dynasties including the Carnegies, the Rockefellers, and the Vanderbilts, she reported. Most of the family's giving flows through the Walton Family Foundation, which Sam and Helen Walton started in 1987. In 2024 alone, the foundation awarded nearly $550 million in grants. The Walton Family Foundation's prime focus areas include the environment, education, and other causes in Northwest Arkansas.

Tom sits on the Walton Family Foundation's four-member board, and Olivia (who married into the Walton family) focuses mostly on the arts and women's causes. She succeeded Alice Walton (the only daughter of Sam and Helen Walton) as the chair of the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville, and she founded Ingeborg Investments, which funds female startup founders. In 2021, she and Tom also helped seed a $1 million fund supporting LGBTQ+ groups in Arkansas, which was a notable move in a conservative state.

Olivia and Tom's latest $100 million commitment is a campaign betting maternal health is one of the few issues that can still draw bipartisan support.

A national poll of more than 1,000 registered and likely voters released in July found 86% of voters say maternal health needs to improve, and 79% would vote for a candidate who champions such reforms. All 15 policy proposals the poll tested drew majority support from Republicans, Democrats, and independents.

Meanwhile, HMHBA is backing two bipartisan bills, the first being the Rural Obstetrics Readiness Act, which is sponsored by Sens. Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Susan Collins (R-Maine), Katie Britt (R-Ala.), and Tina Smith (D-Minn.). This would fund training, equipment, and teleconsultation so rural facilities without obstetricians can handle delivery emergencies. It cleared the Senate health committee in July and now awaits a floor vote.

The second bill, the NIH IMPROVE Act—led in the Senate by Britt and Sen. Cory Booker (D-N.J.)—would authorize seven years of funding for the National Institutes of Health's maternal-health research initiative.

"America should be the safest place in the world to have a baby," Olivia Walton said in a statement. "We have the evidence and we have the solutions. Now we need the urgency and investment to make them available to every mom, across the country."

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

title: Irish Open moved as tour confirms 2027 schedule
description: The Irish Open will take place in early July next year as the DP World Tour announced its schedule for 2027.
fullText:
The Irish Open will take place in early July next year as the DP World Tour announced its schedule for 2027.

The tournament, which was won by Shane Lowry at Doonbeg last week, has been moved to 1-4 July because of the Ryder Cup, which is scheduled for 17-19 September.

With the Ryder Cup's slightly earlier date in September, the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth will be played the week following the biennial contest between Europe and United States at Adare Manor in Ireland.

As a result, the French Open will move to 7-9 September.

The Irish Open was previously held in July before moving to September in 2023.

Next year, it will be played at the K Club before the Scottish Open and Open Championship, and will come at a key time in the European Ryder Cup qualifying process, which will conclude at the British Masters on 22 August.

"I'll obviously be there, I'll play," McIlroy told BBC Sport NI when asked about the Irish Open's new date during last week's tournament.

"Field wise, we'll see, I'm not sure. The Scottish Open will be the week after and a lot of guys are probably going to play that.

"But I get it. The Ryder Cup's in Ireland next year and something had to give."

The DP World Tour's 2027 schedule - which features 42 tournaments in 24 countries - will also include three returning events with the Hong Kong Open, the Singapore Open and Open de Portugal.

The season begins this year at the Australian PGA Championship in Sydney on 26-29 November and will conclude with the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai on 11-14 November 2027.

title: Fiji declares HIV emergency. One in 60 people now have the virus as drug crisis fuels outbreak
description: The small Pacific nation of Fiji has declared a national HIV emergency as it grapples with surging case numbers, partly driven by a growing methamphetamine problem.
fullText:
The small Pacific nation of Fiji has declared a national HIV emergency as it grapples with surging case numbers, partly driven by a growing methamphetamine problem.

One in every 60 adults in the archipelago of less than a million people are now estimated to have Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) –– bucking a global trend of falling rates of the incurable, but treatable, virus.

A tourism hotspot famed for its friendly culture, white-sand beaches and teeming coral reefs, Fiji first declared an outbreak of the virus in January 2025 and ramped up testing, revealing the scale of the spiraling public health crisis.

Declaring the emergency on Tuesday, Health Minister Dr. Atonio Lalabalavu said the country had 2,060 new diagnoses of HIV in 2025, calling it a sign of the "seriousness of the epidemic and the urgent, coordinated response our country now needs."

The epidemic has reached the country's newborns, with a two-month-old baby becoming the youngest identified patient living with both HIV and tuberculosis (TB), Save the Children Fiji said this week. HIV attacks the immune system and makes it easier to contract TB. Last year, 59 babies acquired HIV from their mother, the organization said.

Five years ago, one in 167 Fijians were estimated to be living with HIV. But in recent years, Fiji has seen a surge in intravenous drug use as the islands have emerged as a crucial transit point for narcotics being trafficked from the Americas to lucrative markets in Australia, New Zealand, and parts of Asia.

This, along with persistent sexual transmission spurred by low condom use and stigma, has made the outbreak difficult to tackle.

The alarming statistics do not capture the full scale of the crisis, said Renata Ram, Fiji adviser for the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS).

"What concerns me most is the speed of the epidemic and the number of people who may be living with HIV without knowing it," Ram told CNN.

Only around 39% of people living with HIV in Fiji know their status, and less than a quarter (22%) are on treatment, Ram said.

When left untreated, the virus can progress to Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS), making the body highly susceptible to fatal illnesses and cancers.

Fiji reported 117 HIV-related deaths in 2025, up from 25 in 2021, according to national health statistics.

Fiji's HIV crisis is caused by multiple factors, "but injecting drug use has become a major and rapidly accelerating route of transmission," Ram said, adding that it is common to share needles.

Massive stockpiles of methamphetamine smuggled onto the islands by cartels have seeped into the local communities, spurring a widespread addiction crisis and straining the local health system.

In 2025, people who inject drugs made up roughly half of new HIV cases in Fiji where a transmission mode was identified, while the other half contracted the virus through sexual transmission, according to national health statistics.

Ram said low condom use, multiple sexual partners, limited testing and stigma are contributing factors.

HIV is spread through the exchange of body fluids from an infected person into the bloodstream of an uninfected person.

One in 50 pregnant women in Fiji are infected with the virus, said Lalabalavu, the health minister. Infected mothers can also pass HIV to their infants during pregnancy, labor and delivery, and breastfeeding.

Fiji's growing epidemic bucks the trend globally, where enormous progress has been made against HIV.

UNAIDS estimates the number of new HIV infections worldwide has declined by an estimated 42% between 2010 and 2025, Ram said.

"Fiji has experienced an extraordinary increase over essentially the same period," Ram said.

Fiji's low rate of people receiving treatment also stands in contrast to the global average, where 78% of people with HIV are accessing treatment.

HIV is "not only a health issue," said Joeli Colati, executive director of Fiji Network Plus, a community organization that supports and advocates for people who are HIV positive.

"It's also connected to stigma, poverty, transport, confidentiality, fear."

Colati, who has been living with HIV for 19 years, said there are many reasons why someone may be hesitant to get treatment.

"The reason is not always that somebody does not want treatment," he said. "It can be fear of being recognized at the HIV clinic."

Fiji is a deeply religious society, where premarital or casual sex is generally considered taboo.

Colati said there is also a major information gap about HIV in Fiji, with many people not understanding how the virus is transmitted or how effective treatment can be.

In his address Tuesday, Lalabalavu said Fiji will be moving "quickly" to respond to the emergency, expanding testing, treatment and access to pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) –– a preventative medication –– as well as introducing a formal needle and syringe program.

"I ask anyone who may have been exposed to HIV, including through sharing needles or other injecting equipment, or sex without a condom, to come forward for testing. Do not wait until you feel unwell."

Lalabalavu also encouraged Fijians not to shame, exclude or threaten anyone because of their HIV status, saying "stigma drives people away from the very services that can help them."

Colati said he knows firsthand what "treatment, support and hope can do."

"Please don't let fear make decisions for you," he said. "Knowing your HIV status gives you the power to do something about it."

title: Bevan to play at fly-half in Wales' WXV opener
description: Keira Bevan is to switch half-back roles after being selected to play at 10 for Wales' WXV opener against South Africa in Cardiff on Friday.
fullText:
Keira Bevan will switch half-back roles after being selected to play at 10 for Wales' WXV opener against South Africa in Cardiff on Friday.

The 29-year-old has been training at fly-half during pre-season and will partner Seren Lockwood.

Wales' regular 10, Lleucu George, is named among the replacements, while Kayleigh Powell is no longer an option having been ruled out of the campaign with a hamstring injury.

Head coach Sean Lynn has included three uncapped players in his matchday squad, with Amy Williams named on the wing having impressed in a two-try display in June's uncapped Barbarians fixture.

Front row forwards Elan Jones and Shanelle Williams are poised to win first caps from the bench.

Live on BBC One, iPlayer and the BBC Sport website and app, with live text coverage

Co-captains Alex Callender and Kate Williams will make a rare appearance together having overcome injuries, and are joined in the back row by Bryonie King.

Maisie Davies is given the nod ahead of Gwenllian Pyrs at loose-head prop, and packs downs in the front row with Kelsey Jones and Sisilia Tuipulotu.

Georgia Evans and Branwen Metcalfe are named as locks.

In a reshuffed back line, Lisa Neumann moves to full-back, with Seren Singleton named on the other wing.

Courtney Keight and Freya Bell form a new-look centre partnership with Carys Cox unavailable for selection.

There is no place in the matchday squad for the experienced Bethan Lewis and Hannah Dallavalle, who have both previously captained the side, while three-time Olympian Jasmine Joyce also misses out.

Lynn described his team selection as "exciting" and said the new half-back partnership had been "working very well".

"We know how much of a threat Seren was in the the Barbarians fixture and Keira has been very good in training," he said.

"When she (Bevan) played in the Bristol Bears game [at 10], she looked very comfortable there

"From being a nine, she's used to being the general and will boss that on and off the pitch and drive our attack as well."

Lynn says he is also excited by his back three, particularly Neumann at full-back.

"We've got to get Lisa Neumann with hands on ball, she is such a running threat," he added.

"She's been working on her backfield positioning and has got a pretty big boot as well, and if you're looking at the last line of defence, you don't get any more physical than Lisa Neumann."

South Africa make four changes to the starting line-up defeated 46-17 by New Zealand a fortnight ago as they seek to build depth with the 2029 World Cup in mind.

Felicia Jacobs comes in at scrum-half and Maria Tshiremba on the wing with Maceala Samboya at outside centre as their WXV campaign kicks off.

Logan Welman starts at number eight while Sinelitha Noxeke's status as a utility forward has given the Springboks the chance to opt for a 6-2 bench split.

Co-coach Franzel September said: "We are well under way towards the 2029 Women's Rugby World Cup, not only in our planning, but also giving players experience at the highest level, something that this WXV Global Series will provide.

"This opening weekend is important for us, as we need to set the tone for the remaining two matches."

Wales: Neumann; Singleton, Keight, Bell, A Williams; Bevan, Lockwood; Davies, K Jones, Tuipulotu, B Metcalfe, Evans, K Williams (co-capt), Callender (co-capt), King.

Replacements: S Williams, G Pyrs, E Jones, Crabb, Aiono, A Joyce, George, De Vera.

South Africa: Dolf; Tshiremba, Samboya, Ngwevu, Malinga; Van Rensburg, Felicia Jacobs; Charlie, Gwala, Latsha, Ubisi, Lochner, Solontsi, Catha Jacobs, Welman.

Replacements: Gunter, Khuzwayo, Mdliki, Mokwai, Hele, Noxeke, Cilliers, Mokone.

title: Harwood-Bellis has chance to make his mark at Villa
description: Left out of Aston Villa's Champions League squad and yet to feature since his arrival, Taylor Harwood-Bellis has the chance to shine in the EFL Cup.
fullText:
"His time is coming," said Unai Emery when asked about Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

The £30m defender has had to wait for his chance at Aston Villa following his move from Southampton but now has the opportunity to prove his worth.

He is expected to make his debut against Coventry in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, having endured a frustrating start to life at Villa Park.

Left out of the Champions League squad and yet to feature since his arrival, the 24-year-old has already had his patience tested just over two weeks after joining.

Bought to replace Ezri Konsa after his £51m move to Arsenal, Harwood-Bellis comes in as Villa need stability at the back following a damaging weekend.

Villa conceded 22 shots against Nottingham Forest in Saturday's 2-1 defeat, following the 21 in the opening weekend collapse at Brighton.

Forest's expected goals was 1.92 and Villa won just 35.3% of their tackles.

They also lost Pau Torres and left-back Ian Maatsen to injury - Maatsen's late ankle problem left Villa down to 10 men after Emery used all his substitutes before Igor Jesus scored a late winner.

Maatsen is sidelined until November and Torres' hamstring problem will keep him out for three weeks, with the visit of Brentford on 10 October after the international break a potential return date.

Matty Cash has also been nursing a muscle problem, which kept him out of the 3-2 Champions League win at Club Brugge and Saturday's loss against his former club.

It means it will be a untried defence at CBS Arena on Wednesday, with left-back Matteo Ruggeri likely to make his full debut alongside former Manchester City youngster Harwood-Bellis.

Victor Lindelof has started all six of Villa's games so far, including the Super Cup defeat by Paris St-Germain last month, so should be rested at Coventry.

It is the problem Emery faces, trying to integrate his new players while needing to get quick results following Villa's poor start to the season.

He has faith in his players but the pressure will be on for Harwood-Bellis - who scored on his only England appearance, against the Republic of Ireland in 2024 - to perform as he returns to the Premier League after a chastening previous campaign in the top flight.

With Southampton in 2024-25, when the Saints managed just 12 points and finished bottom of the Premier League, Harwood-Bellis made four errors leading to goals.

That season he made an average of 0.9 tackles a game, compared to Konsa's 1.0 and made 1.4 blocks and 4.5 clearances per 90 minutes, in a struggling team.

A ball-playing centre-back, he made an average of 67.6 passes per game, comfortably clear of Konsa's 50.

Last season, as Southampton were kicked out of the Championship play-offs following the Spygate scandal, he made 7.4 clearances per game, 0.8 tackles and 0.9 interceptions.

Along with young striker Brian Madjo and fellow defender Modou Cisse, Harwood-Bellis was left out for Europe by Emery as the head coach failed to find room.

It has happened before, with Donyell Malen and Andres Garcia last season - Malen eventually left for Roma last January as he looked for more playing time and responsibility.

Emery is banking on the flexibility of Lamare Bogarde and Boubacar Kamara to fill in at the back if his defence is stretched, although that will be of little comfort to Harwood-Bellis.

"Because in Europe you can have 23 players and in the league not," Emery said. "[Mikel] Arteta wanted to open it for more players. We needed to take off someone, and it was Taylor.

"It is hard, the decision we took, and for the players. The experience we have here, when we were without Malen, Andres. To decide, it is through the analysis of how we are expecting to be until January.

"We are going to play eight matches. Cisse is not in because he is injured. Madjo is still injured for the next two weeks minimum. Taylor arrived as the last one, and we can get the balance with Lamare Bogarde, and we can even play Kamara.

"We tried to analyse it deeply. Taylor will be here for a long time, and hopefully, we will have the opportunity to play in Europe with us, in January maybe, and the next few years."

title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda
description: Teenage brothers Olly and Seb Fisher are closing in on their dream of international recognition - but it won't come from their homeland of Scotland.
fullText:
Teenage brothers Olly and Seb Fisher are closing in on their dream of international recognition - but it won't come from their homeland of Scotland.

Instead, the Partick Thistle duo are in line to play for Uganda.

They believe they would become the first white players ever to represent the African nation, thanks to their mother Kate being born there.

"My gran and grandad lived out here for, I think, four or five years," Olly, 18, tells BBC Sport Scotland. "My grandfather came out here to teach in a school then my mum was born here. So, it's a bit of a strange one."

The siblings became aware of interest from Uganda about six months ago, following a chance conversation some time before between their father and a football consultant at a game in Nigeria.

And, at the start of August, they were invited to attend under-20 and under-17s training camps.

They spent last week in Jinja in the country's eastern region and will stay on for one more week, with the pair saying they're "shocked" and "honoured" at the call-ups.

"I couldn't believe it," 16-year-old striker Seb said. "It's one of those things you look at and you're shocked. You can't believe it. Most other people couldn't as well."

Goalkeeper Olly had a similar reaction. "A real mixture of emotions," he said. "I was quite shocked. I didn't really think that this was a possibility but I was honoured to be asked to represent Uganda. I thought it was a real big opportunity."

Mum Kate is "ecstatic" and "thinks it'd be a great experience for us", adds Seb.

There is another Scottish link with Uganda, with former Hearts and Ghana midfielder Laryea Kingston currently coach of Uganda's under-20s.

And he is the one who believes the Fisher brothers are on the verge of making history.

"Coach Kingston was saying we'd be the first white boys to play for Uganda, which would be history in the making," Seb explained. "It is very special."

And Olly added: "It's never been done before, so definitely it is very special."

The pair feel like they're making connections with the African nation, having been reared on stories about Uganda from their grandparents.

And even though they have been training in oppressively warm conditions, they are embracing the opportunity.

"Everyone has been brilliant, welcoming, really great," Seb said. "The other boys have been brand new with us. Some of the boys actually come from the same area where my mum was born. So, they were all talking about that."

The boys will return to Scotland soon, combining training and playing with Thistle with university and school, but are planning to rejoin their new international team-mates in the near future.

Olly hopes to be part of his squad if they qualify for the Under-20's Africa Cup of Nations early next year, and Seb could be in the Under-17 squad for November's World Cup in Qatar.

"That's what you want as a footballer, being in an international environment," Seb said. "It makes you a better player and hopefully it does for the two of us, and I think it will, and benefit us very much going back to Scotland playing at Thistle."

title: Maresca criticises focus on controversial Manchester derby winner
description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says it is "quite poor" that the controversy surrounding Erling Haaland's winner has overshadowed his side's win at Manchester United.
fullText:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca says it is "quite poor" that the controversy surrounding Erling Haaland's winner has overshadowed his side's performance at Manchester United on Sunday.

Haaland's goal on the hour mark, which was awarded after the virtual assistant referee ruled in City's favour, secured a 1-0 Premier League victory despite the visitors playing the majority of the derby at Old Trafford with 10 men following Phil Foden's red card.

The VAR decision was subsequently ruled to be incorrect by the referees' body and the aftermath of City's fourth successive league win has been dominated by the fall out from the incident.

"Talking about one episode or one moment after that game when we played for 70- 75 minutes with 10 players, I think it's quite poor," Maresca said, speaking before Thursday's Carabao Cup third-round tie against Norwich City.

"I think the performance was unbelievable, and I'm pleased with the performance."

Haaland's goal was initially disallowed on the field for offside but the VAR review found the striker was just onside, and the goal was awarded.

However, it soon became apparent that the officials had made an error in failing to identify an offside offence by Enzo Fernandez, diving at the ball in a central position and interfering with opponents.

"There is knowledge that there was a mistake and that's all. Sometimes it goes for you, sometimes against you. It's football," the Italian said.

Maresca, who succeeded Pep Guardiola in the summer, said previous VAR decisions have gone against City, including in a 2-1 defeat by United in January 2023.

"Three years ago when I was here [as Guardiola's assistant], it happened the exact same against United," he said.

"The goal was not a regular goal and no one apologised. We are still waiting for the apology for that."

Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief Howard Webb has admitted the VAR did not consider whether Fernandez was offside before Haaland turned home the winner.

"I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are," said Webb, speaking on 'Match Officials Mic'd Up'.

"None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they're obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation."

Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes in the 23rd minute and United hit the post either side of half-time before the Norwegian's controversial goal on Sunday.

"The VAR gets super-focused on Haaland," said Webb. "He establishes he's onside, he thinks that's a good goal.

"He doesn't truly evaluate the full impact of Fernandez's position. He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score."

City host Norwich on Thursday (19:30 BST) before returning to league action against Sunderland on Sunday, 20 September (14:00).

title: Trump lashes out at Supreme Court justices, saying his appointees ‘are not the people I interviewed’
description: President Donald Trump upbraided Supreme Court justices as “shells” beholden to “crazed” liberal interests in a lengthy online screed a day after the court blocked his plan to execute dramatic changes...
fullText:
President Donald Trump upbraided Supreme Court justices as "shells" beholden to "crazed" liberal interests in a lengthy online screed a day after the court blocked his plan to execute dramatic changes to mail-in voting ahead of the midterms.

"These are not the people I interviewed to serve on the United States Supreme Court, they are merely a shell of their original selves," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Tuesday.

None of the justices Trump appointed to the court during his first term — Brett Kavanaugh, Neil Gorsuch or Amy Coney Barrett — noted disagreement with the majority opinion blocking the mail-voting changes.

Two justices, Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas, said they would have allowed the rules to go into place.

Trump, furious at the decision, decried a number of other rulings handed down by the court that blocked aspects of his agenda. That includes rejections of his plans to limit birthright citizenship and enact sweeping tariffs.

He said the court was "costing the United States Trillions of Dollars with shockingly bad rulings that are of such magnitude that it won't be easily possible for our Country to recover or heal."

"It is a Court that will go down as having rendered some of the most destructive, hurtful, and damaging decisions in our Country's history," he wrote. "It is not easy for me to write this criticism of the United States Supreme Court - it will likely cost me dearly for years to come - but I feel it my obligation and duty, as President, to do so for the America we love!"

The Supreme Court did not respond to a request for comment on Trump's post.

Later Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said the administration would comply with the latest Supreme Court order, though didn't rule out trying to pursue changes to mail voting in the years before the 2028 presidential election.

"President Trump's efforts to make sure that we have free and fair elections are not going to stop just in November or after or thereafter. So I expect you're going to see that work continue," he said.

Blanche defended Trump's harsh criticism of the justices, describing the president as "very frustrated" by the ruling.

"He has every right, and indeed he should communicate his concerns with the Supreme Court whenever he has them. This isn't the first time that he's done it, and it won't be the last," Blanche said.

Despite Trump's protestations, the Supreme Court has handed him significant wins, including a 2024 ruling that found presidents have broad criminal immunity for official acts.

The court also recently allowed construction to continue on Trump's White House ballroom project after preservationists sued to have the work halted.

Still, Trump has grown disillusioned with the conservative justices he appointed that have not ruled in his favor during his second term.

"The Supreme Court has really let our Country down!" he wrote Tuesday. "Certain Justices are petrified of these crazed and depraved Democrats, and are totally unable to show the courage necessary to save our America."

title: 'Mini Valverde' wanted by Chelsea - Garner is now Everton's main man
description: BBC Sport examines how James Garner has become Everton's most important player.
fullText:
Crunching tackles that help win hard-fought away points in an all-action performance are the kind of things Everton fans have become well accustomed to when watching James Garner.

Now the rest of the Premier League are starting to take proper notice.

Following Everton's goalless draw at Tottenham on Saturday, during which midfielder Garner bested a home line-up boasting the near-£200m midfield pairing of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, Match of the Day pundit Thomas Frank hailed Garner's display.

It featured crucial challenges on Tonali and Fernandes to halt promising home attacks - by a player who missed a significant part of pre-season after hernia surgery.

"Garner today was extremely good," said Frank. "He is aware; he's talking; he's organising.

"In a high-press situation, he does the recovery, and that's just so exceptional and so important when you are playing against a team who are dominating you.

"He was running so hard, so that's one side of his game, but also so important is his touches. He is a lot on the ball. It's through him that a lot of things are happening."

Fellow pundit and former Everton defender Ashley Williams said: "He's really impressive. If you're a centre-back behind him, he's the type of midfielder you want."

Garner was signed for an initial fee of only £9m from Manchester United in 2022, having spent the previous season on loan helping Nottingham Forest get promoted to the Premier League.

The academy graduate did not make a Premier League start for United.

After taking two seasons to settle at Everton under Frank Lampard and then Sean Dyche amid a backdrop of financial problems and points deductions, the 2025-26 campaign proved to be a watershed moment.

Garner played all but six minutes of Everton's Premier League campaign to spearhead a European push that lasted for much of the season.

In December Everton travelled to Forest with a depleted squad and won 2-0 to move within four points of the top four.

Garner scored Everton's opening goal in a commanding display that underlined his development.

Following that win, manager David Moyes said: "When I came in, I still saw a bit of a boy and I think I now see someone who's turning into a really good leader as well, beginning to take a bit more responsibility and grow up and begin to start to act like a real midfield player."

The data backs up Garner's growing maturity.

He ranked top for a host of metrics for Everton last season, in terms of creativity and physicality, making the most successful passes, tackles and interceptions, but also providing the most assists and engineering the most chances.

Perhaps most impressively, he stepped up in the absence of key winger Jack Grealish - four of Garner's seven assists came after Grealish's season was ended by injury in January.

"He's been fantastic since I came in," said Moyes. "I didn't realise probably how good he was. He's been so good."

Garner's consistent displays last season earned him a first England cap in a friendly against Uruguay in March.

He produced a man-of-the-match performance, topping the game for tackles and chances created.

After the match England manager Thomas Tuchel compared him with Uruguay and Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde.

"He's our mini Valverde," said Tuchel. "He played very, very good. I was quite sure that he will play good because he has this natural confidence and he's just very physical. He won a lot of balls."

Garner missed out on a place in England's World Cup squad, but those physical attributes could result in more caps in the near future.

He covered the most ground of any Premier League player last season - and 6km more than England midfielder Elliot Anderson - while also topping the overall rankings for tackles and interceptions.

Garner signed a new Everton deal in January, keeping him at the club until 2030, but that did not stop a £65m bid from Chelsea on deadline day this summer, which was rejected by Everton - an important decision given that Garner's versatility is likely to be crucial to a threadbare squad this season.

Everton can currently call on only 17 fit senior outfield players, with Christian Norgaard and Merlin Rohl sidelined because of injury, meaning gaps may have to be plugged throughout the campaign.

Garner has played at right-back and left-back for Everton in addition to his usual central midfield role.

He also played at right-back when England Under-21s won the European Championship three years ago, while Moyes has said he can operate as a number eight or six – a valuable commodity after losing 254 Premier League appearances in the guise of departed midfielder Idrissa Gueye this summer.

If Everton are to push back towards European football this season, Garner may well be their most important asset.

title: Winter Olympic venues confirmed with events in two countries
description: The sporting venues for the 2030 Winter Games are confirmed, with events to be held in Lyon and the French Alps - except speed skating, which will take place in the Netherlands.
fullText:
The sporting venues for the 2030 Winter Games have been confirmed, with events to be held in Lyon and the French Alps - except speed skating, which will take place in the Netherlands.

Events will take place at 11 competition venues, external primarily across southern France with the location allocation for ice sports and alpine skiing confirmed by the International Olympic Committee (IOC)on Wednesday.

Lyon will host curling, figure skating and short track speed skating across three sites, including Parc Olympique Lyonnais, the home of the Ligue 1 side.

Courchevel will host the Alpine skiing speed events – the downhill and super-G, including team events – while Val d'Isere stages the slalom events.

The announcement finalises the venues after a turbulent few months for 2030 Games organisers, which included several changes to original plans.

In May, they were forced to move the Games' 'ice sports hub' to Lyon from Nice after the south coast city's mayor, Eric Ciotti, refused to allow Nice's football stadium to be converted into a temporary ice rink.

And last month, Edgar Grospiron left his position as president of the organising committee just 18 months after his appointment following a turbulent reign amid budget cuts for the Games.

It was also confirmed in May that the long track speed skating events will take place at the Thialf arena in Heerenveen, The Netherlands.

Holding the speed skating in a pre-existing arena outside France was a condition agreed with the IOC when French Alps were awarded the Games in order to reduce costs, as organisers do not want to build new venues that would not have a definite legacy in the host region.

It is the first time that an Olympic event - summer or winter - will be held in a different independent nation to the host city or region.

There will be 16 different sporting disciplines, external at French Alps 2030, with freeride skiing and snowboarding, plus synchro9 - synchronised figure skating - added to the Winter Olympics for the first time.

However the 2030 Games will be the first not to feature nordic combined after the sport was removed from the programme.

title: AG Blanche unveils federal charges against 160 defendants in pandemic relief sweep
description: The Justice Department announced 160 arrests tied to over $245 million in COVID fraud losses, plus a $10 million childcare scheme in California.
fullText:
The Justice Department has charged dozens of people for suspected fraud related to the COVID-19 pandemic that resulted in hundreds of millions of dollars in losses, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Tuesday.

Speaking with reporters in the White House Rose Garden, Blanche said that between mid-June and September, federal prosecutors from across the country helped facilitate the arrests of 160 criminal defendants, including around 80 who were newly charged over suspected COVID fraud in Missouri and neighboring states.

The suspected crimes involved more than $245 million in losses, Blanche said.

White House Launches Interactive Map Tracking Billions In Suspected Fraud

In addition, federal prosecutors in Southern California announced on Tuesday that 12 defendants operating at-home childcare facilities were charged with fraudulently collecting more than $10 million in government childcare payments, despite the operators having few or no children attending their facilities.

All 12 defendants were naturalized citizens from Syria, Afghanistan, Sudan, Iraq and Somalia.

Exclusive: Video Shows Michigan Lawmaker Touring Daycare In $1.1M Taxpayer Funding Probe

"If you knowingly break the law, you will be held accountable," Blanche said.

Some of the defendants were allegedly not even in the U.S. when they allegedly submitted claims for childcare payments.

One defendant, Turkiya Alawad, 63, was found to be outside the U.S. between Jan. 1, 2024, and Jan. 30, 2024. However, they submitted and collected childcare payments for the dates she was not away, prosecutors said, according to The Associated Press.

Minnesota's Eye-popping Subsidy Payments To Nine Daycare Centers Exposed After Last Week's Fed Raids

The alleged daycare fraud case in California is larger than the one involving Feeding Our Future, which submitted roughly $4.6 million in claims to the Child Care Assistance Program in Minnesota, according to The AP.

The Trump administration has prioritized investigating and prosecuting fraud and abuse of government programs.

Vice President JD Vance chairs the administration's fraud task force, which has led to dozens of arrests by prosecutors nationwide.

title: Charlotte to host WTA Finals from 2027
description: The WTA Finals will take place in the American city of Charlotte from 2027 on a three-year deal.
fullText:
The American city of Charlotte in North Carolina has been chosen as the new home of the season-ending WTA Finals.

The WTA says it wants to create the "Super Bowl of women's sports" and is hoping the three-year deal will bring more stability to an event that has had six hosts in seven years.

A planned 10-year stay in Shenzhen ended after just one year, with Guadalajara, Fort Worth, Cancun and Riyadh all taking turns since. Crowds have often been disappointing.

"The WTA has always owned the WTA Finals, but now we are going to operate it, too," said WTA chair Valerie Camillo.

"We are not going to do everything ourselves, but we are taking control of this event, of the creation of the revenue and the controlling of the expenses. And that allows us to control our own destiny."

This year's Finals will be held in Indian Wells, California, before the tournament moves to Charlotte from 2027.

Prize money is yet to be announced, but the pot for this year's Finals will be $10m (£7.4m) - which is $5.5m (£4.1m) less than the sum put up by Saudi Arabia last year.

"2026 is a year of transition for the WTA," Camillo said.

"We are doing the normal belt tightening you would expect of any business while also absorbing the unexpected cost of relocating the WTA Finals to Indian Wells.

"What is most important to know is that we have a clear path to deliver consistent, sustainable financial performance in 2027 and beyond, supported by strong revenue and audience growth."

Riyadh had been due to stage the Finals for a third time in November, but the arrangement finished one year early.

This was partly because of the instability caused by the conflict between the United States and Iran, but also reflected the waning interest of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF).

The country's sovereign wealth fund has recently stopped bankrolling LIV Golf, while the Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters was another casualty earlier this year.

The Finals, which involve the best eight singles players and doubles teams of the year, will be staged at the Spectrum Centre where the Charlotte Hornets play their home NBA games.

The basketball season will be in full swing next November and, because of the frequency of home games, the Finals will be reduced from eight days to five, which is likely to affect revenue.

Camillo says the WTA has already started exploring alternative formats with the players, but if the round-robin element of the tournament survives, the finalists would need to play every day.

The WTA will also move its global headquarters from St Petersburg in Florida to Charlotte as part of the agreement.

title: What's gone wrong for Chelsea talent Kendry Paez?
description: Kendry Paez was one of the world's best young talents when Chelsea signed him as a 16-year-old. Three years later, he's playing for the Under-21s. So what has gone wrong?
fullText:
Attacking midfielder Kendry Paez has finally pulled on a Chelsea shirt, three years after agreeing a move to Stamford Bridge - albeit for the club's Under-21s.

Chelsea agreed a £17.27m deal to sign Paez from Ecuadorian side Independiente del Valle in 2023 when he was 16, but his development has not progressed as quickly as many expected.

Now 19, Paez made his first appearance in Chelsea colours for Cobham Next Gen, the club's newly-renamed Under-21 side, as a 12th-minute substitute in a 4-1 win away to Arsenal on Saturday.

It comes after new manager Xabi Alonso said the midfielder was "not in my plans" and Chelsea listed him as an academy player on the club website.

Chelsea explored the possibility of a loan move in English football, but Fifa regulations left the club unable to send him overseas after using all six of their available international loan slots.

With 27 caps for Ecuador, an appearance at this summer's World Cup and a reputation as one of South America's brightest young talents alongside Blues team-mate Estevao Willian, what has happened to Paez?

Paez is a record breaker and a headline maker.

He became the youngest debutant and goalscorer in Ecuadorian top-flight history at the age of 15 before making his debut in the Copa Libertadores, South America's equivalent of the Champions League, later that same season.

Later in 2023, aged 16 years and 131 days, he made his second appearance for Ecuador, becoming the second-youngest South American international to feature in World Cup qualifying after Diego Maradona.

A month later, he became the youngest South American to score in a World Cup qualifier in a 2-1 win away to Bolivia.

It was understandable, therefore, that Chelsea believed the attacker, who had two international goals and 18 caps when they agreed to sign him, was destined for big things.

Chelsea allowed him to train regularly with the first team before he was officially eligible to join the club following his 18th birthday.

They also provided security for Paez, his family and the family of international team-mate Moises Caicedo after violence broke out in Ecuador in early 2024.

A few months later, Paez was filmed in a New York strip club while away on international duty.

He initially impressed on loan at Chelsea's sister club Strasbourg by winning September's Young Player of the Month award in the French top flight, but then came in for criticism from then-manager Liam Rosenior.

"We expect more, clearly," Rosenior said later that season. "I'm tired of using the excuse of the player's youth."

Despite Strasbourg's links to Chelsea through their shared ownership, the loan was cut short after one goal in 21 appearances. Instead, he joined Argentine giants River Plate on a two-year loan spell.

Sources in Argentina expressed similar concerns about his attitude when asked by BBC Sport. They point to a disappointing display in the 1-0 Superclasico defeat by fierce rivals Boca Juniors at the Monumental in April.

Shortly afterwards, Paez was named by club president Stefano Di Carlo as one of 15 players training away from River Plate's first team, although other sources felt he could have been given more opportunities.

His loan ended by mutual consent after Paez scored once in 14 appearances in 461 minutes for River Plate.

Ahead of the international break, concern has been expressed in Ecuador, having built him up as the country's next great attacking talent.

Michel Deller, the owner of Independiente, told Hincha Amarillo: "He's like a son to us. We care about him deeply.

"He's a good kid who's had a tough time and has made decisions that have complicated his life.

"We are always hopeful he'll show his exceptional talent one again but right now, it's up to him to decide what to do with his life."

These concerns are not dismissed completely by Chelsea or Paez's environment. However, there is a belief they are grossly overstated, highlighting he is owed time to grow as a player and person.

There was one reminder of Paez's quality in the dying moments of Cobham Next Gen's (Chelsea Under-21s) defeat at Wycombe Wanderers in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday.

It was an outswinging cross from a short corner routine, which Harrison Bettoni tapped in during added time. He then put in another cross that caused havoc as Chelsea chased an equaliser in front of just 778 fans.

It was a much-needed boost for Spanish-speaking Paez, who appeared to stand alone from the other academy players before kick-off.

He did join in their warm-ups but mostly kept to himself before coming on in the 62nd minute.

Ultimately Chelsea lost, while Paez was a peripheral figure playing as a right-sided No 10, like Cole Palmer, in a system that mirrored Alonso's back-three shape.

That was until his flurry of activity late on.

Although he's not Chelsea's youngest player, Paez has already made 70 appearances for Ecuadorian side Independiente and more than 100 senior matches in total.

It's something he can fall back on in a more than salvageable situation.

Chelsea have been encouraged by his attitude, having him back in the building at Cobham where he has trained in a stable and elite environment.

There is stability around him as family attended his recent match at Wycombe.

The Blues are also now able to monitor his development more closely, while academy matches are regularly attended by scouts from across the English Football League and beyond.

There is optimism from those close to Paez that he can impress and gain a first loan move in England in January, or one of the six international loan spots will become available for him to go overseas again.

It's more than possible he can rediscover the form that attracted Chelsea in the first place and fulfil the immense potential that made him one of South America's most coveted young talents.

title: Fitzpatrick not '100% comfortable' with tour finals in Dubai
description: Matt Fitzpatrick says he is not "100% comfortable" with the prospect of travelling to Dubai for the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in November when he is due to be defending champion.
fullText:
Matt Fitzpatrick says he is not "100% comfortable" with the prospect of travelling to Dubai for the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in November when he is due to be defending champion.

Fitzpatrick is concerned that the United Arab Emirates could be a target in the ongoing conflict between Iran, the United States and Israel.

"You've only got to look at the hotel that got hit earlier this year," Fitzpatrick told BBC Sport. "I was having dinner the week I won in that hotel.

"That's obviously very scary when you think about how it was a few months away but how close you were to that particular spot and for something like that to happen. It's obviously quite scary."

Fitzpatrick would like to see the event switched to a different host country, a decision he called a "no brainer, in my opinion" before adding: "But I'm not a sponsor, I'm not paying the bills and all that sort of stuff.

"I'm sure there's more to it than just the meets the eye."

Led by chief executive Guy Kinnings, DP World Tour officials are assessing safety issues for their final two play-off events in Abu Dhabi and then Dubai.

Both tournaments are backed by key sponsors of the European-based tour and provide a lucrative end to the season for the circuit's leading money winners.

"I think it's annoying, but at the same time, Guy Kinnings can't control what Iran are doing," Fitzpatrick added.

"It is frustrating because as someone who likes to plan and be prepared, it is difficult to kind of figure out what's going on. Obviously, things as they stand are a bit weird over there.

"I can't say I'm like 100% comfortable, but I guess you just have to see nearer the time and, you know, I still need to qualify as well."

Fitzpatrick's Ryder Cup team-mate Shane Lowry said the tour faces important choices over how to end the current season. "They are huge decisions for everyone," said last week's winner of the Irish Open.

"I'm not going to sit here and comment on the whole thing because I think it's up to the powers above to sort that all out. I think if the tournaments are on, the players are going to go. And if they are not, they will find an alternative."

A spokesperson for the DP World Tour said: "We are in constant dialogue with our members and their management teams about the tournaments they play in, but ultimately players' individual schedule choices are a matter for them to decide.

"As far as our play-offs are concerned, it remains our intention to play as scheduled in the UAE but we continue to monitor the situation and take advice from our international travel advisors."

title: Mbappe, Vini and Konate cover up Real's message of support for Ceuta
description: Vini Jnr, Mbappe and Konate cover up Ceuta message of support ahead of Real Madrid's match against Elche.
fullText:
Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Ibrahima Konate rolled up their pre-game T-shirts ahead of Real Madrid's match at Elche on Tuesday to obscure the message of support for the people of Ceuta.

Ceuta is a Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast, bordering Morocco and separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar.

Players from both sides walked on to the pitch at Elche's ground, Martinez Valero, wearing white T-shirts carrying the message "Todos somos caballas" – translated as "We are all Ceutans" – along with references to the Spanish autonomous city.

While most of the players wore the shirts fully, Mbappe, Vinicius and Konate had theirs rolled up to around chest height, obscuring some of the slogan.

Mbappe and Vinicius then removed their shirts before the pre-match handshake, while Konate kept his on for longer. Their team-mates and the Elche players continued to wear the shirts through the pre-match formalities.

This is not the first time Real Madrid have shown support for Ceuta. Before their Champions League meeting with Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu on 8 September, supporters in the south stand displayed cards featuring the coat of arms of the autonomous city, while the rest of the stadium joined the tribute with a round of applause.

The initiative was part of a wider show of support for Ceuta, following a major migration crisis in the Spanish territory after thousands of people entered from Morocco.

At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July. Most swam around a border fence and at least 100 people died during the crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor.

Although most returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or are sleeping on the city's streets and beaches, leading to unrest in the autonomous Spanish city in North Africa.

Locals have expressed safety concerns and some have destroyed shelters and blocked aid being supplied to the migrants.

The representatives of the players have been asked for comment.

The episode came shortly before a dramatic night for Real Madrid, who recovered from surrendering a two-goal lead to beat Elche 3-2, with Carlos Espi scoring the winner in stoppage time.

Mbappe was among Madrid's scorers, while Vinicius started the game.

The pre-match gesture also highlighted the differing approaches among players and clubs to the Ceuta campaign.

Barcelona did not take part in the initiative, while players at other La Liga fixtures had worn the shirts as intended.
