title: US retail sales rebound more than expected in August; import prices surge
description: U.S. retail sales rebounded sharply in August as households boosted purchases of a range of goods while also spending more at restaurants and bars,
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Sept 16 (Reuters) - U.S. retail sales rebounded sharply in August as households boosted purchases of a range of goods while also spending more at restaurants and bars, reinforcing the economy's resilience even as consumers grow more anxious about high inflation.

Strong demand, together with other data on Wednesday showing ‌a surge in import prices last month sealed the argument for a widely anticipated interest rate increase from the Federal Reserve later in the day, economists said.

The ‌reports followed data this month showing producer and consumer prices accelerated in August, while the labor market regained its poise after wobbling through much of summer.

"This reaffirms that the economy is more than capable of handling higher interest ​rates, providing the Fed plenty of scope to hike to get inflation under control," said Bradley Saunders, North America economist at Capital Economics.

Retail sales jumped 1.2% last month, the largest increase since March, after a revised 0.5% drop in July, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast retail sales, which are mostly goods and are not adjusted for inflation, would rebound 0.8% after a previously reported 0.6% drop in July. The decline in July was the first in nine months. Sales increased 6.0% on a year-over-year basis in August.

Last month's increase also partially ‌reflected higher gasoline prices, which lifted receipts at service stations by ⁠3.1%. Households have continued to spend despite stubbornly high inflation because of the oil price shock and supply chain strains from the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. Consumers have, however, become more selective and are seeking lower-priced goods. Consumer sentiment deteriorated this month.

Spending is being supported by steady wage ⁠growth and recent stock market gains. Households are also saving less and tapping into their nest eggs. The broad rise in sales last month was led by a 2.6% increase in receipts at nonstore retailers, likely boosted by households restocking for the new school year as well as the fading drag from an earlier than usual Amazon Prime sales promotion. Sales at clothing stores rose 0.7%, also likely ​lifted ​by back-to-school purchases.

Receipts at vehicle and parts dealers increased 0.6%, while those at furniture stores rose by ​0.9%. Electronics and appliance store sales jumped 1.6%, and receipts at sporting ‌goods, hobby, musical instrument and book retailers were 1.2% higher.

title: Norway faces backlash over 'deeply racist' proposal to jail citizens for West Bank business
description: Critics say Norway's proposed trade ban on Israeli settlements in Judea and Samaria effectively singles out Jews, calling the possible legislation racist.
fullText:
Critics are slamming Norway over new legislation that they say singles out Jews. The proposed law could send individuals to prison for up to three years for knowingly conducting certain forms of business with Israeli communities in the West Bank.

The proposal, introduced by Norway's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, would prohibit the importation of goods originating in Israeli communities in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem and the exportation of goods to those communities. It would also restrict certain real estate transactions, construction and engineering services and investments in businesses headquartered and operating there.

Intentional violations could result in fines, imprisonment for up to three years or both, while negligent violations could carry fines, imprisonment for up to six months or both, according to Section 7 of the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' official consultation document.

Israel's E1 Plan Explained: The Jerusalem-area Corridor Sparking International Backlash

The measure remains under public consultation, with responses due Sept. 19, and has not yet been enacted.

Israeli Ambassador to the United Nations Danny Danon condemned the proposal in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Norway's proposal to criminalize trade with Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria is the latest expression of their obsessive and openly hostile policy toward Israel. Instead of contributing to peace or regional stability, Norway has chosen political grandstanding, selective outrage and punitive measures against Israel," Danon said. "This approach damages bilateral relations, encourages rejectionism, and exposes just how detached Norwegian policy has become from the realities of the Middle East."

The Israeli Foreign Ministry's Northern Europe Department also referred Fox News Digital to a statement it posted on X condemning the proposal.

Us Ambassador Huckabee Slams Extreme Group Of Israeli Settlers For Seizing Palestinian Homes On West Bank

"Norway's legislative proposal to criminalize trade with Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria is the latest example of the Norwegian foreign minister's obsessive anti-Israel activism on the global stage. Norway has repeatedly chosen to sacrifice its bilateral relationship with Israel in favor of one-sided rhetoric and hostile actions that serve domestic interests, undermine efforts to reach peaceful solutions, and are completely detached from the reality in the Middle East."

In response to a request for comment from Fox News Digital, Norway's Ministry of Foreign Affairs referred the outlet to its June 19 press release announcing the proposed legislation. The release states that Israeli settlements violate international law and undermine prospects for a two-state solution in which Israelis and Palestinians can live in peace and freedom.

"By proposing legally binding prohibitions, the government makes it clear that Norwegian citizens and Norwegian companies must not profit from or support activities that help sustain Israel's unlawful settlement activity in Palestine," Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide said in the release.

Eide also said the settlements contribute to "displacement, extreme violence and a situation that makes a peaceful solution impossible."

Un Agency Accused Of Hamas Ties Sees Another European Nation Cut Funding

The ministry cited United Nations Security Council findings and International Court of Justice advisory opinions supporting its position on the settlements' illegality. It said the proposed restrictions would cover imports and exports, property purchases, certain property-related services and acquisitions of businesses with headquarters and production in the settlements, while safeguarding legitimate Palestinian activities and humanitarian assistance.

The proposed legislation would exempt humanitarian activities, as well as transactions the government determines have "sufficient Palestinian ties" and do not contribute to the construction, expansion or maintenance of Israeli communities.

Dag Juliussen, national director of the Norwegian branch of the International Christian Embassy Jerusalem, said that the exemption could permit business with Palestinian residents while criminalizing comparable transactions involving Jewish residents in the same territory.

"The bill is based on a fundamentally misguided understanding of the Middle East conflict, which in turn rests on a rewriting of history," Juliussen said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "In addition, such a law would effectively serve as a reward for terrorism and, at its core, is deeply racist toward Jews."

Christian Zionists Take On Anti-israel 'Propaganda' From Biblical Heartland

The consultation document does not characterize the proposal as targeting Jews. Instead, it says the measure is intended to prevent commercial activity that helps maintain Israeli communities beyond the pre-1967 lines, while shielding qualifying Palestinian commerce and humanitarian assistance.

Under the proposal, exemptions would be evaluated according to the people involved who benefit from the transaction and whether the activity contributes to the construction, expansion or maintenance of an Israeli community.

Juliussen said purchasing agricultural products from Muslim, Christian, Arab or Bedouin residents could be permitted, while purchasing similar products from Jewish residents could become a criminal offense. He argued that the determining factor would effectively be the identity of the seller.

Norway formally recognized a Palestinian state in 2024 and has become one of Israel's strongest European critics since the Hamas-led terrorist attacks of Oct. 7, 2023.

Juliussen warned that the proposed legislation would not bring Israelis and Palestinians closer to peace but could instead deepen divisions and encourage extremist forces in the region.

title: Real Madrid Goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois Wants To Own Sports Teams, Not Just Play For Them
description: Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois spoke to Forbes contributor Sam Leveridge about NXTPLAY, an investment platform, co-founded with Gonzalo Vila.
fullText:
Reaching the elite in any walk of life is no easy task. In the case of Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, he's seeking to turn his ambition and success on the field to achievements off the field through an investment platform, NXTPLAY, which he founded early this year.

The Real Madrid and Belgium goalkeeper has spent his career being managed. Coaches set his schedule, clubs set his value, and for 20 years the job has been to stop the ball, winning the UEFA Champions League twice, not decide where the money goes, but as he edges closer to retirement, that is changing.

NXTPLAY, the investment platform he co-founded with Gonzalo Vila, now holds stakes in three soccer clubs, a lighting and fan-experience partnership with Signify, and a stake in the gaming platform PlayVault. He discussed the company's origins, his own role inside it, and what comes after playing, on the sidelines of the World Football Summit in Madrid, where he and Vila presented NXTPLAY to the industry.

Most soccer players monetize fame through sponsorship deals with brands, ambassadorial roles, or even the occasional restaurant with their name on it. Yet part of NXTPLAY's mission is to bring in more elite athletes to join the group. "Some are more interested in it, some share a vision, and sometimes you need to speak to an entourage, but often they see an opportunity to see what you are doing," Courtois told me in an interview after his panel participation at the Summit.

"Others have brand deals and are less worried about investments, but eventually doing what I do I think I will create more interest when they see that what they do is good and that they can trust me with it," he explains. "Being on LinkedIn, involved in NXTPLAY, I feel like there are more opportunities coming. They see you also as a businessman, maybe they trust me more than a usual footballer."

Rather than going down that road, Courtois has worked with Vila and NXTPLAY to build a company that takes ownership positions. It's not an entirely different proposition to what he does as a player. "One big thing is the ambition to do things well, and the work ethic," he says. "As a professional footballer, you want to do things well and grow. In some deals you can share your vision more clearly, because I've been in this world for 20 years, and in other things I can learn."

He has also worked alongside some of the sport's fiercest leaders, both on the field and on the touchline, and believes that those transferable skills have been crucial to what he can achieve in the business world. "Leadership is something important, the way to delegate and surround yourself with people who understand," he says, citing Gonzalo Vila and the wider team NXTPLAY has assembled. He credits two coaches in particular for shaping how he thinks about building that group. "Learning from people like Ancelotti and Mourinho, who are very different but very good leaders and know how to build a team, that's our goal, to build a dream team."

Of NXTPLAY's three football holdings, KRC Genk, Le Mans FC, and CD Extremadura, only one can claim to be the club that produced Courtois himself. He does not pretend the Genk investment carried the same weight as the others, having come through the ranks at the club having joined them at the age of eight.

"It was an amazing feeling," he says of signing the deal. "I owe everything to them, and the great youth academy which helped me grow into the person and goalkeeper I am today."

That academy has kept producing goalkeepers long after Courtois left it for Chelsea a decade ago. Genk has since sold Mike Penders to Chelsea, Lucca Brughmans to Liverpool, and Senne Lammens to Manchester United, a production line Courtois calls a source of pride rather than nostalgia. That is at the heart of his ambition with Genk, saying, "we want to help companies to grow and become big companies, inside of technology or media, and football teams like Genk to help them become the main players in the Belgian league, we look at Club Brugge as the team to beat with their investment, stadium expansion, but we believe we can compete".

He also revealed a personal ambition. "My dream was always to play against Genk. It's never happened," he says, recalling a near-miss in the 2012 Europa League when the draw kept his Atlético Madrid side apart from them. "A Genk versus Real Madrid Champions League game would be a dream way for me to finish my career."

NXTPLAY's portfolio so far is European, but Courtois says a long-term dream has him watching the United States market, pointing to the scale of recent franchise valuations as evidence of where sport is heading. "The size of sports teams in the U.S. is huge," he says. "You can see they keep growing, and the U.S. sports market is growing. The love I have for those sports makes a great connection. We want to dream big, but it's always a step at a time."

The platform's move into gaming, through its stake in PlayVault, reflects a similar instinct, one Courtois traces back to his own experience streaming during the pandemic. "It's huge," he says of esports' potential. "Everyone can play or follow streams on their phone, it's a way of connecting." He wants NXTPLAY's athletes integrated into the platform directly and name checks a specific ambition: joining the Formula 1 esports grid. "A thirteen or fourteen year old kid with a passion for motorsport can find friends, a place to belong, and fight for a dream. Why can't it end up being a real race car?"

Courtois is not ready to say what NXTPLAY looks like once he stops playing, only that he expects to still be busy combining his love for football and business. "I haven't decided yet," he says. Coaching a first team holds little appeal to him despite holding UEFA's A and B licenses. "I'm not sure I would want to be a coach of a first team, you would get old really fast with all the players."

He is drawn instead to development work, pointing to Genk's academy as a model. "Maybe working in the goalkeeping department at Real Madrid, establishing a top academy, developing a Thibaut Courtois instead of buying one." For now, though, that remains a future project, as he admits, "I still want to play five or six more years."

The five-year plan for NXTPLAY itself is more concrete, if still early. "We want to grow into an important investment vehicle in the world of sport and media," Courtois says, adding that raising a dedicated fund is the next step to reach new markets.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: National high school flag football rankings: USA TODAY Sports Super 25, Week 4
description: After Central's long-standing winning streak was snapped, a new team takes over the top spot.
fullText:
After four weeks atop this list, Alabama powerhouse Central snapped its four-year, 62-game win streak with a 20-12 loss to Merced (CA) this week, leaving the top slot up for grabs, shaking up their own season and catapulting Merced into its Super 25 debut. The typical California powers have maintained their perch at the top of this week's rankings, and North Carolina's Wakefield is on the move after officially kicking off its own season.

More: Merced flag football ends Central-Phenix's historic 62-game winning streak

As more states begin to kick off their seasons this month, here are the USA TODAY Sports Super 25 national flag football rankings for Week 4:

They've finally taken the crown. The Lions land themselves on top of the Super 25 for the first time this week, following the first loss in four years for previous No. 1 Central (AL). They held on to their undefeated record through a busy, five-game week, led nearly flawlessly again by sophomore QB Kate Meier. In their 41-7 win over Santa Margarita (CA) last week, Meier threw for 288 yards and four touchdowns with zero interceptions.

The Lancers get a boost over Newport Harbor this week, holding the line to add four more victories to their tally – including one over previous No. 1 Central (AL). Senior QB Alyssa McClure threw 24-for-32 for 223 yards and three touchdowns in that victory, while sophomore Annie Hoogeveen led on the other side of the ball with seven flag pulls.

The Sailors slip behind Orange Lutheran this week on the back of too-tight victories over Huntington Beach (CA) and Carlsbad (CA) and a loss to JSerra, but they've still been in good form. Newport Harbor's squad has logged wins against Mission Hills, Carlsbad and Corona del Mar since we last spoke, and have a rematch with Huntington Beach coming up Wednesday that we'll definitely be keeping an eye on.

The biggest news of the week came when Central lost not once, but twice, ending its 62-game winning streak at the MaxPreps Flag Football Showdown. After establishing themselves as an Alabama powerhouse the past four years, claiming three-straight AHSAA Class 6A-7A state titles, the Red Devils took their talent to California to face some of the toughest teams in the nation. These losses, however, came to two of the most talented teams in the nation – Merced and Orange Lutheran. While being in the losing column is a new feeling for the Red Devils, don't get used to seeing them there, as they are still one of the most dominant teams in the country.

Willowbrook is still the reigning monarch of Illinois, and it still has yet to drop a game. Senior Kaitlyn Santos has been taking the majority of the snaps, throwing 10-for-15 for 215 yards and three touchdowns vs. Stagg this week, while Madeline Carine also made the most of her time at the helm with two passing touchdowns coming from just six throws. A lot of those balls were headed for Mckenzie Edison, who caught for 247 yards and three TDs in that game.

Not far behind Central lies another Alabama powerhouse in Moody. The Blue Devils handed Vestavia Hills its first loss of the season in a 28-7 victory to continue its undefeated streak. Junior quarterback Serenity Rutledge continues to show off her accuracy and speed, completing 17-of-21 passes for 204 yards and four touchdowns while also adding 134 yards on the ground. Moody followed that game up with another victory, blanking I3 Academy 49-0.

After a disappointing loss to Grandview last week, Mountain Vista bounced back with a crucial statement win over Legend, 33-14, to reclaim the top spot in the Colorado rankings. Junior quarterback Peyton Marr was extremely accurate, completing 28-of-36 passes for 239 yards and three touchdowns. The Golden Eagles' defense, however, might have been the key to this win. The team had four interceptions, two sacks and totaled 28 flag pulls while allowing just two scores in the victory.

Legend took its first loss of the season to Mountain Vista last week in what might have been the top game in Colorado this season. However, the Titans bounced right back with a 68-0 win over Highlands Ranch. Junior quarterback Addyson Law completed 16-of-20 passes for 186 yards and five touchdowns as 11 different receivers got their hands on the ball. Mountain Vista might have been Legend's toughest battle of the regular season, so the Titans will look to keep that their only loss.

Smith's Station made a big jump this week after a massive 54-0 win over JAG. Senior quarterback Brooke Norred had a near-perfect game, completing 19-of-20 passes for 266 yards and seven touchdowns — with six different receivers finding the endzone. The Panthers still have a number of challenging matchups on their schedule, but will look to keep Moody as its only loss of the season.

St. Charles North is on the way up. The North Stars picked up three victories to maintain their perfect record this week, with two of those coming in the form of dominant shutouts. Four different players caught touchdowns in their 33-0 victory over Oswego East, with junior star Alexzandria Richardson doubling up with an additional rushing touchdown.

Huntington Beach suffered a tough, 8-7 loss against Huntington Beach (CA) this week, buffered by wins over San Marcos (CA), McClatchy (CA) and Marina (CA). Next up is already a rematch with Newport Harbor, a great opportunity for the Oilers to move up through the California flag ecosystem if they can squeeze out the win this time.

Flag football in North Carolina is finally up and running, and Wakefield has hit the ground running. Out to a 4-0 start to their season, with three of those four being shutouts, the Wolverines are looking primed for a strong title defense run in the Tar Heel state's first officially sanctioned season.

The Chargers just keep charging. Adding two more dominant wins to their tally this week – 49-0 over Lompoc (CA) and 27-6 over Ventura (CA) – to push up to 12-2, Dos Pueblos is riding a nine-game win streak into next week and primed to keep crawling up the rankings.

The Bears storm into the Super 25 this week, fresh off a headline-making victory over Central (AL) that ended the previous four-year, 62-game winning streak. Senior Averie Steverson was all over the field against the Bobcats, logging 10 receptions for 127 yards and three touchdowns. They've strung together a pretty strong, 12-2 season so far, with the main outlier being a close loss to Los Gatos (CA) this week. We'll be eager to see if their season keeps heading in the right direction.

Dimond earned a huge 6-0 overtime win over former No. 13 South Anchorage last week, earning it a spot in this week's rankings. Sophomore quarterback Emaani Fleming has yet to throw an interception this season and has averaged 46.1 yards per game on the ground through ten games. The Lynx now remain as the only undefeated team in Alaska with just eight games left in the regular season. Later this month, however will be a crucial rematch between Dimond and South Anchorage.

The Titans remain perfect at the midpoint in the season after grabbing wins from Coronado and Fountain-Fort Carson in the past week. While they eased past Coronado 52-14, Fountain-Fort Carson caused them some trouble offensively, as they scored their lowest amount of points all season. However, a win is a win, and The Classical Academy continues to do just that.

It was a tough week for Vestavia Hills, as it earned its first two losses of the season to Moody and Oak Mountain. With Vestavia Hills' starting quarterback Eden Logan still out with a leg injury, the Rebels have struggled to find poise and momentum — especially on offense. Freshman Alana Anderegg has taken over at the helm, but the Rebels are still searching for ways to win without their star player.

Not only did South Anchorage allow its first points of the season, but it also suffered its first loss to Dimond in a battle of two undefeated teams. While the Wolverines only lost 6-0 in overtime, the offense was limited all game, totaling just 143 yards. The two teams will face off once again at the end of the month, as the Lynx will try to even the matchup.

title: OU football loss, Oklahoma State upset show why college football is best show | Mussatto
description: Last Saturday was a reminder of why college football is the best show going.
fullText:
Boone Pickens Stadium erupted when the final from Ann Arbor was announced.

The Bedlam football series is dormant, but Sooners and Cowboys fans still take delight in the others' demise.

Oklahoma State's massive upset of Oregon coupled with a disappointing OU defeat gave the Pokes a reason to gloat. They earned it after enduring two years of misery. OU fans, meanwhile, had three reasons to grieve: an OU loss, an OSU win and an improbable Texas comeback against Ohio State.

More: What Oklahoma State football players, coach thought of fans storming field vs Oregon

Last Saturday was a reminder of why college football is the best show going.

The NFL product is more consistent, and way more balanced, but that leads to a lack of upsets. The Cardinals beating the Chargers was the NFL's version of an underdog story in Week 1.

College football is filled with games that aren't fair fights. It's why we can't stop talking about Western Michigan almost beating Michigan. Which makes OU's loss to Michigan all the more dispiriting. Western Michigan > OU??? Of course not, but the Broncos can make the case!

What happened in Stillwater was wild. The Cowboys were 24.5-point underdogs! Oregon was 57-0 straight up since 1978 when favored by 24 or more points, according to ESPN, and OSU had lost 21 consecutive games against FBS opponents. And the Cowboys were clearly the better team, at least for one Saturday.

Which maybe means that Tulsa is good? Maybe not. The Golden Hurricane barely survived its trip to Huntsville, Texas. OK, so maybe Sam Houston State is decent. Except that Sam Houston State lost to Troy.

See, we can go around and around trying to make sense of results that don't make any.

"It's why you play the game," OSU athletic director Chad Weiberg told The Oklahoman.

Let's get to the rest of this week's Minutes:

More: OU football's defense has a tackling problem. How Michigan exposed Sooners

Despite the schools being in bordering states, Oklahoma and New Mexico have only played twice. And not since FDR was in office. OU beat New Mexico 47-0 in 1930 and 25-0 in 1935. Both games were in Norman.

New Mexico is 2-0, outscoring opponents 108-14. The opponents were Central Michigan and FCS Mercyhurst. Bonus points if you knew that Mercyhurst is the Lakers. Or that it's in Erie, Pennsylvania.

Speaking of nicknames, New Mexico became the Lobos in 1920. The name was chosen by the editor of the student newspaper, who was also a manager for the football team. "The Lobo is respected for his cunning, feared for his prowess, and is the leader of the pack," a 1920 edition of the newspaper read. New Mexico's colors are cherry and silver.

Jason Eck is in his second season as New Mexico's coach after a successful three-year stint at FCS Idaho. Eck, last season, led the Lobos to their first bowl game since 2016.

After losing starter Jack Layne in the preseason, the Lobos have alternated between Oregon transfer Luke Moga and Toa Fa'avae at quarterback. Neither has thrown the ball much. The Lobos haven't needed to throw.

Murray State University, OSU's upcoming opponent, is in Murray, Kentucky — 627 miles from Murray State College in Tishomingo. Our Murray State only plays flag football.

OSU has Bullet. Murray State has Racer 1. Since 1985, Murray State's live horse mascot has run a lap around the Stewart Stadium track after every Racer touchdown. Murray State's original nickname was the Thoroughbreds. The school adopted Racers in the late 1950s.

Murray State is a basketball school. The Racers have made 18 NCAA Tournaments, including eight since 2000. They advanced to the Round of 32 in 2022 and 2019. Ja Morant starred on the 2019 team.

The Racers are 3-24 under third-year coach Jody Wright, who was the tight ends coach at South Carolina before taking the Murray State job. He was Alabama's director of player personnel from 2015-17 — a three-year stretch in which the Crimson Tide won two national championships.

Murray State's last game against a Big 12 opponent was in 2022 against Texas Tech. The Red Raiders beat the Racers 63-10.

Against all odds, Oklahoma State's winning streak in home openers reached 31 games.

That's the longest such streak in the nation, according to OSU public relations.

Looking at OSU's future schedules, the streak will at least reach 33 games. OSU's next two home openers are against Western Illinois in 2027 and Southeastern Louisiana in 2028 — a couple of FCS pushovers.

Then, in 2029, Tulsa comes to Stillwater for the opener. That, as recent history has shown, is no gimme.

OSU's last home-opening loss was to No. 2 Nebraska on Aug. 31, 1995.

During the 31-game streak, OSU has only played four power-conference opponents: Oregon (2026), Washington State (2010), Georgia (2009), Mississippi State (1998).

Lane Johnson, RT, Eagles: Johnson announced that this season, his 14th in the NFL, will likely be his last. The 36-year-old Philly lifer remains one of the best tackles in the league. He was the Eagles' highest-graded offensive lineman in their 24-22 win against the Commanders, according to Pro Football Focus.

Chuba Hubbard, RB, Panthers: Hubbard had one rushing touchdown and one receiving touchdown in the Panthers' 59-37 loss to the Bears. He had 49 rushing yards and 38 receiving yards. Hubbard is in his sixth NFL season, all with the Panthers. Hubbard has 24 career rushing touchdowns, tied with Chris Carson for fourth most among former Cowboys.

Kip Lewis injury update: OU football LB receives 'good news' on injury

Here are my OU and OSU picks for the week.

Sandwiched between road trips to Michigan and Georgia, this had the makings of a trap game. But then a couple of things happened. First, New Mexico quarterback Jack Layne, the returning starter from a nine-win team, underwent season-ending elbow surgery. And then OU lost at Michigan, which means New Mexico will have the Sooners' attention more so than if OU was 2-0 with a clash in Athens upcoming. I'm picking a comfortable OU win, but give me the Lobos plus the points.

Picking the Sooners this season: 1-1 straight up, 1-1 against the spread

I had to access the dark corners of the internet to find an OSU-Murray State line. That's a sign that we should all stay away. (But if I had to pick a side … Murray State, it is. That's a whole lot of points).

Picking the Cowboys this season: 1-1 straight up, 1-1 against the spread

Joe Mussatto is a sports columnist for The Oklahoman. Have a story idea for Joe? Email him at jmussatto@oklahoman.com. Support Joe's work and that of other Oklahoman journalists by purchasing a digital subscription today at subscribe.oklahoman.com.

title: England winger Freeman signs new Northampton deal
description: Northampton Saints and England winger Tommy Freeman agrees a contract extension with the reigning Prem champions.
fullText:
England winger Tommy Freeman has signed a new contract with Prem champions Northampton Saints, keeping him at Franklin's Gardens "for the foreseeable future".

The 25-year-old made his Saints debut in 2019 and has gone on to make 118 appearances for the club across all competitions, scoring 79 tries.

He scored Saints' opening try in their 2024 Premiership final win over Bath and repeated the feat in their 2026 triumph over Exeter Chiefs.

"Its a no-brainer in terms of the coaching staff we've got," Freeman told BBC Radio Northampton.

"I think I'm going to grow as a player here. I don't think anywhere else at the moment is going to help me do that.

"I'm performing with England as well and involved in that, and that's a big credit to Saints - giving me the opportunity and putting me on the stage to do my skills and go and impress."

Freeman's decision to commit his future to Saints follows on from England team-mates Fin Smith, Fraser Dingwall and Alex Mitchell also all agreeing new deals at Northampton - although the future of Henry Pollock remains uncertain.

"You can't really beat the players in and around us, the group of friends we've got, and the coaching staff to help me grow as a player," Freeman added.

"You want to be happy where you're playing. Being a special group, you go on to achieve something special as a group."

Following his England debut in the 2021 autumn internationals, Freeman has won 30 caps, scoring 11 tries. Freeman also made six appearances for the British and Irish Lions on their 2025 tour of Australia, including three Test matches.

Saints' director of rugby Phil Dowson told the club website:, external "To have Tommy commit his future to the club so early in this season's recruitment and retention cycle is a huge boost for us. We're delighted that he's chosen to continue his journey with Northampton Saints."

Freeman has played at both wing and centre for England, and Saints head coach Sam Vesty has not ruled out Freeman featuring more at full-back for his club.

"I think he'll cover more of the backline," Vesty said. "With squads getting that little bit smaller, being able to have a couple of positions to play is a fantastic attribute, and that's one of his big strengths."

The exact duration of Freeman's new deal has not been revealed although he still had one season remaining on his previous contract.

BBC Radio Northampton sports editor Graham McKechnie:

Freeman is without doubt one of Saints' crown jewels, so re-signing him is an important boost before the start of the new season.

There's been so much talk about Pollock's future at Saints, but purely in rugby terms, keeping Freeman in black, green and gold is even more important.

Not only is Freeman one of the best wingers in the world, as he's shown with both the Lions and England, but he's also an important figure off the pitch for Saints.

Like others before him, such as Smith, Mitchell and Dingwall, he's talked about the importance of the bond of friendship they have at the club.

He may well have been able to earn more elsewhere, but having that happy work environment is clearly a big deal for him and others - as well as playing a very exciting brand of rugby.

title: Does Bellamy need to win back Wales fans?
description: After a "sleepless night", Wales boss Craig Bellamy decided to turn down the chance to manage Burnley - but has it affected what fans think of him?
fullText:
The challenge facing Wales is sizeable.

Cristiano Ronaldo in Lisbon, Erling Haaland at home and a double-header with a Denmark side they have not beaten in 18 years as Wales return to Nations League A.

But does head coach Craig Bellamy face his own challenge?

Supporters were already smarting from missing out on the World Cup. Then their mood darkened further as it emerged Bellamy had held talks over becoming boss at Burnley.

The 47-year-old admitted to a "sleepless night" when coming to a decision to either stay with Wales or succeed Scott Parker at Turf Moor, the club he had previously served as an assistant boss under Vincent Kompany.

Bellamy said he went with his gut to turn down Burnley and that he had unfinished business with his national side.

Nevertheless, some pundits have suggested the 78-cap former striker now needs to win back support after such speculation over his future.

Bellamy suggested he did not know whether that is the situation he faces over the next three weeks - and beyond - after reiterating his ambition to lead Wales to a home Euro 2028.

Even so, given that as a player Bellamy once had a legal tussle with his club in order to be available for his country, is it fair to question his commitment?

Bellamy 'committed' to Wales after Burnley talks

Rodon absent as Ashford earns first Wales call-up

Bellamy: 'I made the decision to stay'

Bellamy says he has a "gift" of not taking what people say to heart, but he will have heard queries over his commitment before.

"I think with my body of work over the years, I don't think I need to say too much about that," he said, after announcing his squad for the first four games of the new Nations League campaign – the first international matches since the Burnley saga.

"I think my commitment has always been there and I've proven that over the years.

"I remember I had to go and get solicitors' letters from independent people because my club at the time were trying to tell me not to play [for Wales] and they would sue me if I did. I haven't seen anyone else do that."

There are other examples of Bellamy's commitment to Welsh football.

He donated money to Wrexham when they were in financial difficulty during his playing days, while there have been claims that he has not claimed expenses from the Football Association of Wales (FAW) either as a Wales player or coach.

"Wales is way more important to me," he said. "I don't believe I have to ever try to win anyone over with that."

But has the Burnley episode changed that?

Bellamy has denied that his decision not to join the club side was based on an issue with backroom staff. He says that instead it came down to what he felt was right, and that he left a lucrative offer on the table.

He suspected that Burnley had expected him to take the job and felt there was surprise and disappointment when he said no.

"I had a sleepless night because I knew it had become real," added Bellamy.

"I have to be honest, I woke up in the morning and it wasn't there. I didn't have that feeling of going into a meeting and grabbing it.

"You don't know until that moment comes, but to me, it has to mean the most to me."

But is that enough for some? Or - as Bellamy himself has suggested - will it take a return to winning ways and putting World Cup disappointment to bed to fully draw a line under things?

Ryan March, Wales regular and editor of fanzine Alternative Wales:

"We obviously don't know what goes on behind closed doors - and if what is being reported is gospel, or what Bellamy himself says is fact.

"So, it all depends on what or who you believe, but the fact is Craig Bellamy now has even more work to do to get the fans back on side.

"We all saw that Bosnia-Herzegovina game as a huge missed opportunity [to reach a World Cup finals] and, for most of us, the blame lies at Craig Bellamy's door for his game management.

"The summer's friendlies only added to that frustration as we lacked any sort of performance - and most fans were OK with the idea of him going to Burnley.

"The only way Bellamy can truly win the fans back ahead of next year's Euro 2028 campaign is by winning games and [producing] good performances. That's the simple fact.

"If we go and win a few of these Nations League games and stay in Group A, the flirtations with Burnley will be a distant memory."

Rob Earnshaw, former Wales striker and Match of the Day Wales pundit:

"I'm glad that he's still here because I think he moves Wales forward if he's in charge.

"There's always going to be Wales fans that are looking for the manager to impress them, looking for the manager to do more.

"The only thing that I know he can control is if he wins games - and things will be better. So that's the aim, but that's going to be difficult with some big games coming up.

"The only other thing that I can speak for, knowing and understanding Craig, is that his commitment won't change with Wales.

"If we were talking about two clubs, maybe that would be different. But with Wales, the commitment doesn't change.

"His drive to make the team better, make players better, trying to win us games, is going be the same - and that's going to be relentless.'

Sam Vokes, former Wales striker:

"I think he (Bellamy) is the right person to lead us into the next two years, leading up to Euro 2028 and a home tournament.

"I know he wants to walk that team out in that competition.

"I think he's made the right decision. Hopefully they can park this now, he can move on. We have some important games in the Nations League coming up.

"We were unfortunate to miss out on qualification through penalties last summer. I think those players will come in, as players do, crack on with their job and move on from this.

"In terms of the fans, winning games wins fans over. If we do well under Craig moving into this Nations League and the next European qualification, happy days because that's what fans want to see."

title: Why are Man Utd better without the ball?
description: Under Michael Carrick, Manchester United average 1.5 points per game when they have more than 50% of the ball. When they have less than 50%, this number is 2.6.
fullText:
Under Michael Carrick, Manchester United average only 1.5 points per game when they have more than 50% of the ball. When they have less than 50%, this number shoots up to 2.6.

And if you drop possession further, to 45% or below, United have won 10 games out of the past 10 since the start of last season.

It is a staggering correlation but it brings the Englishman to the same crossroads that former United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer found himself at.

How do you bridge the game from a seemingly elite counter-attacking side to one capable of beating teams that give you the ball?

The answer has long eluded United.

Going down to 10 men on the way to a 1-0 derby defeat is far from ideal, but at full-time Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca offered a different perspective.

"We had a plan for 11 versus 11, but after the red card the game completely changed, but also for them.

"They love transitions and space in behind, but the game became more difficult.

"We just dropped, [offering] no space in behind and no more transitions, which is why the game was also more difficult for them."

This was an astute analysis of United's most recent game as well as their team this year.

As divisive as the phrase "United DNA" is, it undoubtedly remains a key part of the conversation about United both externally and internally.

This is because certain coaches have leaned into the club's roots, while others have tried but failed to move away from those ideas.

"We want to win; we want to be excited - that's why we love this club. I'm fully aware that we need to do it in a certain way," said Carrick when asked what style of football he wanted his United side to play.

Here he echoed the sentiment of United's most successful manager, Sir Alex Ferguson, who in 2017 said: "You have a duty to entertain. We have to always remember there's a public to be entertained."

With excitement seemingly non-negotiable for Ferguson, it is obvious why fans and players of that era resonate with a United that create spectacles.

Dynamic, direct and open games are sought after to remain connected to a United they recognise.

Solsjkaer's side embodied United's DNA before Ruben Amorim looked to play a more choreographed and risk-averse style of play. Carrick went back in the opposite direction.

Having established the context, we can take a closer look at how this has manifested on the pitch.

With the messaging around Carrick's style of play being one of proactivity, excitement and directness, it is no surprise that United look better with space to attack – something that happens more often for a team with less of the ball.

The strengths of the squad are suited to this approach, with goalkeeper Senne Lammens a good long kicker of the ball. In defenders Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez, United have punchy progressive passers from deep too.

In attack, Marcus Rashford is a willing runner in behind, often moving into a striker position despite starting on the wing. The same can be said for Bryan Mbeumo.

Bruno Fernandes, central to all of this, is a strong passer when attacking in transition, finding runners ahead of him – a role in which he broke the Premier League assist record last term.

Carrick has also provided certain players a level of freedom to make their own decisions on the pitch.

"Giving Bruno the platform to go and perform [has helped him]," Carrick said in April.

"We're trying to create a structure to try to bring out the best of everyone, but I like seeing Bruno in attacking positions with a bit of freedom."

Although players may enjoy this responsibility, how the team play can be swayed by individual players' natural tendencies.

With more risk-taking, direct passers in the side, when United are asked to disorganise stubborn defences their long-standing habits can mean losing the ball more often.

When dominating the ball, breaking down a team requires strong one-against-one wingers. Defending teams often clog the centre of the pitch, as City did in the derby, forcing the attacking side to the flank.

City's Jeremy Doku, Arsenal's Bukayo Saka, Bayern Munich's Michael Olise and Paris St-Germain's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia have been key in helping those sides win often – while keeping the ball.

This season United have used a 4-2-4 shape in possession. The full-backs have pushed up and taken turns with the wingers to hold wide or narrow positions.

This, however, often results in Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu, Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo – not the strongest one-v-one dribblers - isolated on the wing.

Amorim used a system without wingers and the squad built as a result – with the exception of Rashford and Amad Diallo – appear underprepared to create chances from out wide.

With wide play an area of concern, play is often funnelled back infield.

Carrick has primarily used Fernandes and Matheus Cunha as a floating front two, both with licence to drop deep or pull wider.

Both players are more suited to facing the opposition's goal, rather than playing with their back to goal in small spaces, which makes it hard for United to capitalise through the middle.

City's Rayan Cherki and Arsenal's Kai Havertz are players suited to this role, albeit in different ways.

Fernandes and Cunha's quality means they can still be effective in these positions, often forming triangles with the full-back and wingers, helping United get into the final third.

But as they both vacate the striker position, United end up lacking bodies in the box when they play crosses in.

The best teams have repeatable methods of chance creation in the final third that suit their players' strengths. Teams then cycle through these depending on what the opposition are offering them.

With United's attackers given more freedom, they often seem to be looking to solutions during the game more reactively compared to the more repeatable methods of creation Maresca can fall back on.

With United struggling to beat teams that allow them the ball, their impressive set-pieces provided them with a workaround last season.

Since Carrick took over, 56% of United's opening goals have come from corners, free-kicks or penalties, and 28% from Casemiro's headers.

After scoring, opponents are more likely to attack, which stretches the game, allowing United to play to their strengths and in a more direct fashion.

This season they have not shown that same prowess and, although Casemiro is known for his defending, the loss of his ability to help open the scoring makes United's attacking concerns against deep defences a more pressing issue to address.

title: Woods seen on range for first time since car crash
description: Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago.
fullText:
Tiger Woods says he "can hit pretty much anything" after returning to the range for the first time since a car crash six months ago.

The 15-time major champion was seen hitting balls at Liberty National in New Jersey in a video shared on his Instagram, external before the Nexus Cup, a charity event he is hosting to raise funds for his TGR Foundation.

Woods, 50, also held a clinic where he was asked by the master of ceremonies about his game and replied: "I can hit pretty much anything."

It comes six months after the golfer rolled his Land Rover in Florida and had to crawl out of the passenger door of the car. He refused a urine test.

Earlier this month, Woods accepted a five-year suspension of his driving licence and a $1,000 (£742) fine, as part of a plea agreement with prosecutors in Martin County, Florida, after not contesting a reckless driving charge.

It remains unclear whether Woods is preparing for a comeback.

He has not played competitively since 2024 after rupturing an Achilles tendon in March 2025 and having back surgery last October.

After March's road accident - his second arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence - Woods said he was "stepping away for a period of time to seek treatment and focus on my health".

It was the latest in a string of incidents that have littered Woods' recent years.

His marriage ended - as did lucrative sponsorship deals - after he struck a fire hydrant, a tree and several hedges outside his home in a 2009 incident, sparking accusations of extra-marital affairs.

In 2017, he was sentenced to a year's probation after pleading guilty to reckless driving. That came after police officers found Woods slumped at the wheel of his car near his home.

In 2021, Woods survived a serious accident which left him with extensive injuries and he played only a limited schedule since then.

title: Released despite seven straight wins, baffled Mokaev vows UFC return
description: Muhammad Mokaev tells BBC Sport that he is still searching for answers about why he was cut by the UFC in 2024 and dreams of returning to the organisation.
fullText:
It has been more than two years since Muhammad Mokaev was released by the UFC - and yet he is still searching for answers.

In July 2024 the Russian-born Briton had just stretched his winning run in the promotion to seven fights with a unanimous decision victory over Manuel Kape at UFC 304.

From the outside, Mokaev appeared to have it all.

Victory over Kape in Manchester had seemingly further cemented his place as a top contender in the flyweight division and a title shot appeared to be within his grasp.

But later that night UFC president Dana White made the shock announcement they would not be re-signing Mokaev.

It was initially suggested Mokaev's behaviour in the build-up to facing Kape – which included clashes with his Portuguese rival at the fighter hotel and again at the weigh-ins – may have influenced the UFC's decision.

According to Mokaev, that is not true.

"If we talk about behaviour, right - if I'm a bad guy, why would you let me fight seven fights and renew my contract twice?" Mokaev told BBC Sport.

"If I'm a bad guy in the company and organisation, they would cut me after one or two fights."

The flyweight, who moved to Britain as a refugee when he was 12 years old, believes his wrestling-heavy style was a contributing factor.

Mokaev won his UFC debut via submission in just 58 seconds before beating Charles Johnson by unanimous decision in his second bout.

He says the UFC text his manager after that victory over Johnson saying "he needs to stop wrestling - we don't want these decision guy".

"I have around a 60% finish rate in the UFC. Four out of seven fights were finishes against top guys," Mokaev said.

"I don't know what else I need to do to show them - I was 21 when I was fighting these veterans and now I'm much better and much stronger.

"From 21 to 23, I beat all these guys. Even Manuel Kape, and he is ranked number two right now. I really don't understand the politics. I really don't know. I wish I knew the full story behind everything."

You only need one look at Mokaev's record since July 2024 to understand how determined he is to make his way back to the UFC.

Few fighters on the planet have been more active than the flyweight, who has competed eight times over the past two years.

Since leaving the promotion, he has finished opponents with chokes, body kicks, head kicks and punches, while also winning titles in BRAVE CF and ACBJJ.

Yet it has not been enough to catch the attention of UFC matchmakers Hunter Campbell, Mick Maynard and Sean Shelby.

Although Mokaev is in a WhatsApp group with Campbell and Shelby, he believes the UFC is constantly moving the goalposts.

"Hunter made me a promise. They basically wasted two years of my life," Mokaev explained. "That's how I feel right now. I don't think what they are doing is right."

Mokaev says he was also offered $10,000 (£7,399) to compete in UFC BJJ, a Brazilian jiu-jitsu competition, against bantamweight champion Mikey Musumeci.

Despite finding the proposed fee deeply insulting, he was willing to face the five-time world champion if the UFC offered him a contract afterwards.

"They said, 'no, this is different. BJJ is different. This is different. We have other plans.' I told them where to go," said Mokaev, who admitted his response to the UFC contained several expletives.

When Joshua Van defends his flyweight title in a rematch with Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331 in Los Angeles, California, on Saturday, there will be a sense of what might have been for Mokaev.

That is because Van, 24, became the first UFC champion born in the 2000s when he defeated Pantoja in December.

It was a feat that had long looked likely to be achieved by Mokaev after he signed with the UFC in 2021 and quickly soared through the ranks.

Only former UFC champions Demetrious Johnson (13) and Pantoja (eight) have recorded longer winning streaks in the flyweight division than Mokaev (seven).

It is why he remains steadfast in his belief that he is the best flyweight in the world and that he will one day have UFC gold around his waist, even if it comes later than he anticipated.

"The way I'm going to compete and keep winning, eventually they're going to send me there," Mokaev said.

"Back then I said, 'the best fight the best.' But it doesn't matter what happens with the situation, I think I'm the best flyweight in the world and I deserve to fight the best."

It is also part of the reason he has decided to sign one-fight deals rather than committing to longer-term contracts.

There have been more lucrative, multi-fight contracts offered to Mokaev since 2024, though he will only consider signing them if the UFC's stance on his return does not soften.

One of those offers came from the Professional Fighters League (PFL) to fight in its bantamweight division, as the promotion does not currently have a men's flyweight division.

Mokaev says he would be tempted to put pen to paper if the PFL created a 125-pound division following its merger with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions in July.

"I want to stay active because I'm still young. I just turned 26. Most people start their careers at this age," Mokaev said.

"I'm going to do what's best for my family."

title: 'He's an idiot, but he's our idiot' - Saints fans on Pollock contract stand-off
description: How has a drawn-out and public contract negotiation affected the relationship between Henry Pollock and Northampton Saints fans?
fullText:
Henry Pollock is determined not to blink first in his contractual face-off.

Despite a deal with Northampton being close, amid reports of an agreement of about £400,000 a year,, external the back row stressed on Monday that his renewal was not signed.

He is, he says, still open to offers.

Asked if he was looking forward to the end of the saga, stoked by Pollock's advisor Eddie Hearn, Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson joked that "it would have been good to have it sorted three weeks ago".

The haggling has certainly played out more publicly than most negotiations.

Has it taken some of the sheen off a player who was key to Saints winning the Prem title last season and whose public profile has brought new supporters and attention, not just to his club but to his sport in general?

Lis Saunders is the chair of the Northampton Saints Supporters Group.

"I have known Henry coming up through the academy and he is absolutely delightful," she told BBC Sport.

"The perception of his arrogance is wrong. He is just a young bouncy man, living his best life.

"Some people are getting a bit fed up with the whole theatre around [the contract stand-off], though.

"I am laissez-faire about it. If he stays it will be brilliant, but you can't keep someone who wants to go.

"The whole theatre around it is what will grind people's gears. You are starting to see that on some of the fan forums – people saying, 'Either sign or don't. Just don't mess around - we don't need this drama.'"

Saunders points out that, while Pollock can pull a crowd, Saints invariably fill Franklin's Gardens anyway. The turnstiles will carry on clicking at the same rate regardless of his presence.

It would be an emotional wrench rather than a financial loss if he moves elsewhere.

"As the players themselves say, he's an idiot, but he's our idiot," said Saunders.

"We've watched him grow up and he's very much ours. It would be really sad if he didn't stay - perhaps understandable, but really sad."

Charles McGillivray is one of the hosts of Beneath the Lift Tower,, external a Northampton Saints podcast run by fans and named after the landmark that looms over Franklin's Gardens.

He says the stand-off has split fans, even if Pollock, who was superb at the end of last season, still has the support of the majority.

"There are probably two ends of the spectrum," he said.

"You've got some fans who are just reading headlines, may not be as engaged as others and don't really understand the mechanics of how rugby clubs in England work, with the salary cap and things like that.

"But most Saints fans are fairly grounded. They understand that Eddie Hearn coming to Henry Pollock's career is going to be brilliant for the sport and together they're going to make lots of noise.

"And they also understand that the money being quoted [Hearn says Pollock is worth £1m a season] isn't really feasible to be earned by someone in England.

"We think he's a grounded - if ambitious - lad and therefore Northampton is the best place for him to be.

"There isn't a club in England at the moment developing talent at the rate of knots or to the level that Northampton is. And maybe only Bath are having the continued success that Northampton are having."

McGillivray's co-host Simon Stacey, who has been following the club for 40 years, points out that Northampton fans have seen first hand the risks that players run for their rewards.

In 2018 Saints centre Rob Horne went in for a hard but routine tackle and incurred nerve damage that cost him the use of his right arm.

"I don't hold any grudges against Henry," said Stacey. "It doesn't annoy me. I get that they do need to get what they can because it's a short career and they have to look after themselves."

With a club's spending on salaries capped at £6.4m - with another £1.4m available in various credits and compensations - a bumper pay deal for one player at a Prem club reduces the money available for others.

Last autumn scrum-half Alex Mitchell said he and others had prioritised the togetherness, external and quality of Saints' squad over "mega money" elsewhere when opting to re-sign.

While Northampton did not pay up to the salary cap in the most recent report on Prem club finances, which covers the 2024-25 season, a raft of renewals is likely to take them closer to the limit in the coming years.

However, if Pollock's stance is causing ructions in the squad, they are hiding it well.

Fly-half Fin Smith momentarily joined Hearn in lobbying for Pollock to be granted a £1m annual salary this month, telling reporters that "he's worth it" before joking that Pollock had sent him out to do a bit of PR on his behalf.

Dowson dropped a request into the squad's group chat, asking if the squad could borrow the private jet Hearn had laid on for Pollock to visit him on the French Rivera.

As Pollock gave an interview on Monday, soberly stressing that the forthcoming season could be his last at the club, his straight face briefly broke as Mitchell smirked at him from across the room.

Hearn has said he found Pollock's current earnings at Northampton, thought to be about £150,000 a year, to be unbelievable. And not in a good way.

Certainly, Pollock, one of the faces of the sport, is due a significant pay raise.

The league's latest salary cap report is revealing.

His current salary is below that of the 2024-25 league average of £191,000.

Of the players in his current age bracket (20-22) that season, 27% were paid more than he is now.

Pollock has 13 England caps. The average wage of a player with 11-20 caps was £224,000.

Even if he finalises his reported extension, it will be at a lower level than the average 'marquee' player – those whose pay is excluded from the salary cap – took home in 2024-25. That figure was £533,000.

Finn Russell, the Scotland fly-half and only other rugby player who is part of Hearn's Matchroom stable, is one of those marquee players, on a deal worth about £1m a year with Bath.

Pollock has long since outgrown his current deal, signed in December 2024 before his England debut, Champions Cup knockout heroics and British and Irish Lions call-up.

The obvious destination were Pollock to move within the Prem.

Backed by Austrian energy drink dynasty, Pollock would be a statement signing that fits their youth-orientated brand. The club had plenty of headroom on the pay roll, spending barely half of the salary cap's upper limit in 2024-25 campaign.

However, a revamp of the playing squad since then will have given them less ability to manoeuvre, and Prem Rugby rules on domestic moves prevent Pollock from being the club's designated marquee player for his first two seasons elsewhere.

Pollock would also have to weigh up whether swapping the Prem champions for the league's bottom club, who are without Champions Cup rugby for 2026-27 at least, is desirable.

French clubs operate under a significantly higher salary cap of 11m euros (£9.4m), and the Top14 is booming, challenging football for prominence in the country.

Thanks to skirmishes with Bordeaux-Begles in the Champions Cup, Pollock has pantomime villain status in the country.

He was jeered the loudest of any player when England played France in Paris in March. His vigorous celebrations of Tommy Freeman's 76th-minute try, which appeared to have clinched the win for the visitors, will have further endeared him to the locals.

However, a move across the Channel would come at the cost of Pollock's England career and the associated central contract, worth about £150,000.

There is also a considerable cultural shock to overcome. Courtney Lawes, a Northampton legend, has just returned to England, saying some aspects of his two-season spell with Brive were challenging.

Henry Arundell, the bright, young thing of English rugby before Pollock, endured a difficult time at Racing 92 before returning to the Prem a year earlier than anticipated.

The money-making move of choice for many of the southern hemisphere's finest.

Richie Mo'unga, Pieter Steph du Toit and Malcolm Marx are among those who have enjoyed the lighter schedule and yen-heavy pay days in Japan.

While England internationals George Kruis and Alex Goode have made moves there in the past, there has been a shift lately to favour Japanese players over big-money imports.

Both Kruis and Goode were near the end of their careers. A switch to such relative obscurity would do little to build Pollock's brand in rugby's major markets.

Perhaps the most intriguing comment made by Pollock this week was a desire to explore "other sports" during his career.

He has been a ringside regular since signing with Matchroom, most recently attending Katie Taylor's farewell fight at Dublin's Croke Park, and chatting with UFC fighter Ian Machado Garry at a recent charity fundraising event.

His high-energy style would suit a switch to rugby league, and it has been reported, external that a number of Super League clubs, buoyed by possible investment from the NRL, are monitoring Pollock's situation.

The big-money start-up circuit, originally slated to begin next month, would surely have been keen on Pollock.

However, it has been postponed until 2028 and, with conflict in the Middle East further unsettling investors and logistics, looks increasingly unlikely to transpire.

title: F1 to have 10 sprint races in 2027, including Monaco
description: Formula 1 increases the number of sprint races from six to 10 for the 2027 World Championship.
fullText:
Formula 1 has increased the number of sprint races from six to 10 for the 2027 World Championship.

Sprint events, which feature a shorter race on Saturday and an extra qualifying session on Friday, will be held for the first time in Bahrain, Australia, Japan, Monaco, and Abu Dhabi.

The other sprints will be in Canada, Britain, Italy, Brazil, and Qatar, it was revealed as the calendar was formally announced.

The maximum number of sprints previously in a season has been six.

The 2027 season is scheduled to start in Bahrain on 12-14 March, followed by Saudi Arabia a week later, but both events will remain in doubt while the war in the Middle East continues.

Bahrain is the default season-opening race, but Australia has hosted the first grand prix for the past two years because of the timing of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan.

The 2026 season is due to end with two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, and while F1 is planning to complete the calendar as scheduled, it is working on contingency plans if those races cannot be held as a result of the continuing conflict between the US/Israel and Iran.

The same applies for the start of next season as F1 considers its options for an alternative opening schedule if racing in the Middle East looks impossible by the end of this year.

On Sunday, a summit involving some of the nations involved in or affected by the conflict released a statement urging "maximum restraint" in the war.

The British Grand Prix will be on 2-4 July, and the 2027 season re-introduces races in Portugal and Turkey, returning for the first time since being used as placeholder events during the pandemic.

Sprint events usually come at a higher price for race organisers but they are in demand because they increase the chance of selling more tickets, with competitive action on each of the three days of the meeting rather than only Saturday and Sunday.

Silverstone believe holding a sprint this year was a large part of the reason for the British Grand Prix’s highest ever attendance - 64,000 more fans attended over the course of the four days compared with the year before, which was not a sprint.

The inclusion of a sprint event in Monaco will inevitably raise eyebrows, given it is almost impossible to overtake around the historic street circuit.

However, F1 is selling it on the fact that it means there will be two qualifying sessions at Monaco - qualifying around the demanding track is renowned as one of the highlights of the season.

Two separate qualifying sessions could also provide two different grid orders, increasing variability.

The flip side of a sprint in Monaco is that, because of the lack of overtaking opportunities, the finishing order of the sprint will be pretty much locked in once the cars have completed the first lap, barring accidents.

F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Turkey to the championship and to expand sprint racing to 10 events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special."

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, the president of F1's governing body the FIA, said: "The 2027 FIA F1 World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport.

"With 24 grands prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Turkey, and the opportunity for an expanded sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

Pre-season testing is also scheduled to be held in Bahrain on 24-27 February.

title: Ranking the greatest all-time fantasy football icons
description: There's nothing quite like the satisfaction of unearthing an absolute Fantasy Premier League bargain - so who are the most iconic picks ever?
fullText:
Scanning the newspaper, inky fingers and fuzzled minds, scrambling for the calculator and jotting down the codes for Julian Dicks and Juninho. These lads will carry the team until you remember to pick up the house phone and cash in a transfer a few months down the line.

Before templates and triple captains there was a world of fantasy football that existed by writing out your XI and ringing in the names. Parents used it as a summer-holiday maths lesson.

Yet whether in print or online, there's nothing quite like the satisfaction of unearthing an absolute bargain. That free-kick taking defender, the undervalued forward, out-of-position goal-getter or cheap keeper posting clean sheets.

Since it began for the 2002-03 season, Fantasy Premier League has evolved into a huge database boasting millions of players across the globe, with substitutions and wildcards and the maths done for you.

But who, over the past quarter of a century of the competition's official game, are the biggest icons of all time?

With the help of our resident FPL expert Thomas Woods and some extensive research by the Fantasy Football Scout, that's what I'm digging into this week.

Based on stats and a touch of sentiment - Michu, we see you - I've ranked my top 10 below. We'd love to hear your thoughts in the comments, too.

Firstly, let's look at what makes a player iconic. Is it purely posting massive numbers? Thierry Henry's total from the inaugural season, for example, still ranks seventh overall. Indeed the Arsenal man was top scorer in three of the first four campaigns, but also the most expensive.

Frank Lampard, arriving late in the box, topped the charts three times with his goals from midfield for Chelsea, while the twinkle-toed Cristiano Ronaldo did it twice at Manchester United. The pair rank fourth and fifth for best individual seasons, respectively.

It's tempting to say we should discount such "obvious" picks for this debate, but then there's Mo Salah. The Liverpool asset might have eaten up a decent chunk of your budget, but packed guaranteed points for those premium pounds.

As the Fantasy Football Scout explains, since the game began, 52 players have reached 200 points in a season at least once. Salah has done it eight times. And the Egyptian is the only player to ever top 300 points. In fact, he's done it twice.

So Mo probably deserves a go. But we're really searching for those who have offered the most value over the years - cheap picks who seriously delivered.

Some went on to become Premier League stars, others became cult heroes, one-season wonders or bargain buys who got virtual tongues wagging.

10. Harry Kane, Tottenham, 2014-15, starting price £5m

England captain and record goalscorer, three-time Premier League Golden Boot winner. Harry Kane was hardly a secret at Tottenham, right?

After a series of loans and having not yet established himself at White Hart Lane, the young Spurs striker began the 2014-15 campaign as a likely £5m back-up to Emmanuel Adebayor and Roberto Soldado.

Kane didn't find the net until November in the Premier League, a 90th-minute winner after coming off the bench at Aston Villa, but it was the first of 21 goals in the competition that season as the homegrown striker established himself in Mauricio Pochettino's side.

As the Fantasy Football Scout notes, an eight-match run from gameweek 18 to 25 saw Kane notch 77 points with nine goals, four assists and 16 bonus points.

For those who gambled on him early, Kane proved a bargain. He rose from £5m to a peak £6.4m, racking up 191 points and ranking 11th on the all-time value list, despite playing fewer minutes than all those above him.

9. Charlie Adam, Blackpool, 2010-11, £5m.

The great budget enabler. Blackpool's Charlie Adam took penalties, free-kicks, corners and would probably have had goalkicks too if they let him.

He'd had a good season in the Championship, scoring 16 times, but no one really gave the Seasiders any hope on their Premier League debut and thus there was little expectation on the Scottish midfielder from FPL bosses.

Despite Ian Holloway's outfit eventually succumbing to the drop, Adam delivered a points tally that was only bettered by Manchester United's Nani that season - on the back of 12 goals, his 192 stood as the highest score by a promoted player at the time.

8. Michel Vorm, Swansea, 2011-12, £4m

Michel Vorm conceded four goals on his Premier League debut. That stacks up for a £4m keeper, you might think. Yet the Dutchman made 11 saves that day at Manchester City, more than anyone else would manage in a single game that season.

Vorm swept Swansea City's end-of-term awards but also became a FPL legend in the process. He made saves but also kept clean sheets, 14 of them in total, and earned the second-most points for a goalkeeper behind City's Joe Hart, who started the game £3m more expensive.

The Dutchman peaked in price at £5.3m and was the fourth-most owned player in the game at one point. Both virtually and in real life, it would be his standout season.

7. Stuart Dallas, Leeds, 2020-21, £4.5m

Under Marcelo Bielsa, Stuart Dallas was a FPL dream.

Racking up defensive clean sheets while operating further forward than his listed position suggested, cheap as you like, and even doing it against league heavyweights Manchester City, where he scored twice for 17 points.

"The Northern Ireland international's versatility played into the hands of FPL managers because, even though he was a classified as a defender, he played all over the place for Leeds in 2000-21 - more often than not as an attacking midfielder," explains Woods.

"And for a starting price of £4.5m you got eight goals, 12 clean sheets, three assists and a total of 171 points. Bargain."

6. Michail Antonio, West Ham, 2019-20, £7m

Michail Antonio is a curious pick, but deserves FPL cult hero status for one of the most memorable months in the game's history.

Classified as a midfielder but deployed up front, Antonio's value actually dropped during a campaign that was disrupted by injury and the coronavirus pandemic.

Following the restart, Antonio was unstoppable. He played seven times in July 2020, scoring eight goals. Incredibly, four of those came in West Ham's 4-0 away win at Norwich, where the midfielder posted a 26-point haul.

That's the joint-most on record for a player valued under £7m, alongside Cole Palmer, and only three off Salah's overall record for a single gameweek.

5. John Lundstram, Sheffield United, 2019-20, £4m

Lord Lundstram, as he was fondly known, didn't notch a season total as high as some on this list, but his bargain price, out-of-position listing and the fact he seemingly appeared from nowhere, having only made five starts for the Blades the previous season, saw him achieve legendary status in FPL.

"A £4m defender is usually the last spot on FPL managers' benches but Lundstram was misclassified by FPL towers and was actually a box-to-box midfielder," says Woods.

"He scored five goals and delivered four assists while picking up clean sheets along the way to 144 points, with his two-goal 21-point haul in week 11 particularly memorable.

"And being able to start a £4m asset allowed managers to cram more talent into the rest of the team too."

4. Riyad Mahrez, Leicester, 2015-16, £5.5m

Riyad Mahrez was a goldmine for Claudio Ranieri and FPL bosses alike during Leicester's title-winning season. As the Fantasy Football Scout notes, he flew out of the blocks with a 15-point haul in week one against Sunderland, rewarding the 5.9% of managers who started the season with the winger in their side.

It was no fluke. Mahrez made double figures in five of the opening six gameweeks, his 56 points among the best starts ever to a FPL campaign. Inevitably, other managers jumped on board, and by week seven Mahrez was in more than 50% of teams.

Jamie Vardy, of course, had a dazzling season of his own, returning a goal or an assist for 15 weeks on the bounce, though he started £0.5m more expensive than his team-mate.

Mahrez finished the campaign as the top scorer in FPL with 240 points, despite his modest starting price.

3. Michu, Swansea, 2012-13, £6.5m

Of course, there is a certain amount of nostalgia and sentiment to FPL. We gaze proudly at these little icons clocking up points like they're family.

Michu was the epitome of an on-screen cult hero, going from relative unknown to bagging 190 points, his price rising by £2m throughout the year.

As Woods says, he is probably the biggest one-season wonder in FPL history.

"A few savvy managers picked up on the fact the Spaniard had scored 15 goals in La Liga the season before and had him on the opening day when he scored twice at QPR," adds our resident FPL expert.

"He was effectively a £6.5m striker classified as a midfielder. It felt like he was in most managers' teams by the time he ended 2012-13 with a whopping 18 goals.

"He managed two the following season... and then left for Napoli."

2. Mohamed Salah, Liverpool, 2024-25, £12.5m

OK, firstly, other Liverpool assets were perhaps unfortunate to miss out on this list - flying full-backs Trent Alexander-Arnold and Andy Robertson were consistently must-have picks.

Luis Suarez, meanwhile, boasts the third-highest score ever and, as the Fantasy Football Scout points out, he notched a record 55 attacking returns in 2013-14 despite missing the first five games.

But if we can allow one premium pick, it has to be Salah. And if we have to pick a season, it must be his record-breaking 2024-25 campaign when the Egyptian produced a staggering 344 points.

Remarkably, it came off the back of his lowest score the year before - although low for Mo was still upwards of 200 points. Salah, simply, is FPL royalty.

1. Cole Palmer, Chelsea, 2023-24, £5m

You have to put Cole Palmer's 2023-24 season into context. He wasn't a household name, like now, having left Manchester City for more gametime at Chelsea.

The youngster began the season as a £5m midfielder and did not start a game for the Blues until matchweek seven. In fact, as the Fantasy Football Scout explains, only 63,575 managers owned him (0.6%) for his first double-figure return at Burnley the following week.

That crept up to 4.5% for his next 12-pointer at Tottenham in gameweek 12, which then triggered a surge in popularity as FPL bosses lumped on Stamford Bridge's new star.

More than five million owned Palmer when he scored four goals against Everton during a 26-point haul in gameweek 33, albeit he still only cost £6.1m.

"Based on starting price, Cole Palmer in 2023-24 is the best-ever value player in Fantasy," concludes the Scout.

Palmer finished as the season's top scorer with 244 points and was handed the biggest price rise in FPL history of £5.5m, meaning he cost £10.5m at the start of the 2024-25 campaign.
